utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. I would like the record to reflect that the late start is due to technical problems in the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-04-75-T, the Prosecutor versus Goran Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. May we have the appearances, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. For the Prosecution, Douglas Stringer, Alex Demirdjian, Case Manager, Thomas Laugel, and legal intern, Lucia Laporte.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Defence. Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For the Defence of Goran Hadzic, Zoran Zivanovic and Christopher Gosnell. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If there's nothing else, then the witness may be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: May I remind that you're still on your oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm afraid I have to go back briefly to Arkan. Probably because I was speaking too quickly on Friday, there was an important word missing from the quotation from General Panic in his interview to the BBC in the Death of Yugoslavia interview. And that was up on the screen in front of you before, so I'm not going to put it up again. I'm just going to put to you the proper quotation and then pose a question to you. And what General Panic said on that occasion in respect of, I suggest to you, the arrival of volunteers in September 1991 was: "They were not big groups, say in Arkan's case between 80 and 120 persons, and in Seselj's case between 90 and 120 men. All these formations were under my command but the people who wanted to act independently were being removed from that area and disarmed and returned home." Now can you agree with me that that implies that Arkan is subordinated to the armed forces continuously in the year 1991, from August to December?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, because as far as I recall the statement by General Panic for the Death of Yugoslavia, he didn't provide a specific time-frame for the -- his statement that all these groups were subordinated to him. I don't dispute the statement. On the contrary, I have included it in my report, but I think Mr. Gosnell now introduces specific dates and those dates are not available or were not pronounced by Mr. Panic in the Death of Yugoslavia interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's go to what you said in the Milosevic case at page 31488, and the end of an answer leads to a question by a Judge and then a clarification on your part. And I'll read it. And these are your words at the beginning and then there's a question from the Judge and then there's your answer: "And that brings us back to the initial distinction that was made: Volunteers as individuals are purely legal, then we have volunteers as groups which were -- or steps were done to subordinate them to the JNA, and then we have individuals or groups like Arkan -- excuse me, like Dragan or Arkan who, again, according to JNA information, actually were related to the Ministry of Interior of Serbia, even if there could be doubts about the legality they were doing, but that's probably outside of my knowledge."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: "So that according to your thesis then, Seselj and his men, Arkan and his men, were within the command structure and subordinate to the lowest level of the JNA?" Answer, this is your answer: "Based -- based, Your Honour, based on the orders I've seen and the order that have been used for the report, the answer to that is affirmative. There were -- they were, indeed, subordinated to JNA units in the framework of the structure I discussed earlier in order to maintain single command." Now no mention there, Mr. Theunens, at all of what you said on Friday about Arkan stepping in and out of subordination during this period, is there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you remind me, Mr. Gosnell, when I made that testimony in the Milosevic trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That was the Milosevic trial. I don't have the exact date noted down but it would have been 2002 or 2003, I believe.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Your Honours, since 2000 -- I don't dispute my testimony, but since 2003 we have obtained additional documents, and these additional documents, I mean specifically SBWS, that was during the Vukovar trial, and these were most documents we requested from FRY and Serbia, these documents allowed to further specify the issue of subordination. And as I've mentioned throughout my testimony and cross-examination also in different -- in other trials where this issue was discussed, as a rule volunteers and paramilitaries should be subordinated to the JNA. To see how the situation was in practice, we have to look at the specific documents, and I have for example quoted from reports by security organs of 1st Military District where it is stated that, I'm paraphrasing now but I recall that stated that, Okay, quote/unquote, it is believed that Arkan acts outside the subordination of the JNA or on the orders of the Ministry of Interior or maintains and/or maintains specific relations with the authorities of the SAO SBWS. You can check the records of the OTP when these reports of security organs became available but not all of those were available at the time I testified in Milosevic trial. And, again, the more documents you look at, the easier it becomes to really see the -- the sequence of events and to also be in a better position to qualify general statements like the subordination of volunteers and paramilitaries to the JNA during combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I thought we agreed on Friday that the OB reports about Arkan were neutral.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, what do you explain -- what do you understand --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: No, excuse me. I just need to finish my question, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I paused because there was a --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- a note from the court reporter. So my question is: I thought we agreed on Friday that the JNA OB reports about Arkan were neutral in respect of the issue of his subordination to the JNA. Now you're saying that they're not neutral, that they show that he's not subordinated?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that -- that is not what I'm saying. I say that there are some reports where -- and I will try to identify them but there are -- there is at least one report, and we discuss it in examination, where it is stated that at least according to the people or the sources interviewed by the security organ that these sources believe that Arkan operates on behalf of the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia. And that I have -- I mean, I also recall that at least one or several of these documents specify that he is not under JNA command at specific instances, but I don't dispute that there are instances and probably for most of the time Arkan operated under the command of the JNA in fall 1991 in SBWS. But I tried so say it's not black or white. There are -- I mean, there are a lot of nuances and that's why there are some many documents I have attempted to review in this report, and for each of conclusions I draw also in relation to subordination there are footnotes to official JNA or other documents to substantiate these -- these conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Isn't the whole point of the notion of singleness of command and command and control that when issues are not black and white the unit is considered subordinated?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honours, and this is visible from the documents, the various orders issued by General Panic for example on the 15th of October as well as on 16th of November where he re-emphasises the importance the JNA maintaining control in the areas it has captured or -- or seized as well as to always subordinate the volunteers and paramilitaries together with other documents we have seen from General Kadijevic, from General Adzic, all these documents show that there were difficulties with the subordination of volunteers/paramilitary groups. One of the reasons is because these -- these groups were not foreseen by law. They popped up or they appeared in certain parts of the disputed areas be it in Eastern Slavonia or Western Slavonia or the Krajina, and JNA commanders faced the problem of what to do with these groups and how to handle them and that's why these additional orders were issued, i.e., to subordinate them or to remove them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yeah. But those orders don't mention Arkan, do they? They mention other groups; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, we can look at specific documents but they mention volunteers groups in general terms. They don't specify the groups. There is one document but that's not so much an order, it's more a report. The armija report by the assistant commander for moral guidance of the 1st Proletarian Guards Mechanised Division, Milan -- Lieutenant-Colonel Milan Eremija when he discusses the crimes in Lovas he mentions, for example, Arkan and he also mentions other groups. But that's not an order, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And even assuming that Arkan is sponsored, supported under the protection in some way of the Serbian MUP, that's in no way inconsistent [Realtime transcript read in error "consistent"] with being subordinated to the JNA, is it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, the transcript say it's is no way consistent or you mean inconsistent?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Inconsistent. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. One doesn't exclude the other, and that's -- again, that's I think visible from the documents I have discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have L43, please. This document, as such, is not on our list; however, it is a part of 01939 which appears on our list twice at Defence tab 77 and 208.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I see we have the wrong document. I feel that I went down this road before with Dr. Neilsen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Perhaps we could just remove that document from the screen and I'll just put a question to you, Mr. Theunens. Mr. Theunens, do you know that it was only on the 18th of August, 1991, that those who were involved in setting up a district government in SBWS promulgated or initiated the process of promulgating laws to set up ministries. Do you know that that was the date, the 18th of August, 1991?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is -- this is probably the case, yeah. I mean, I have the date my report but I don't by heart. Maybe you can point me to the section in my report where I discussed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That's all right. I'm just going to proceed to the next question. And that is do you know that it was only on the 25th of September, 1991, that the statutes were passed by the SBWS Assembly setting up Ministries of Defences, Justice and so forth?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, I have to reason to doubt the date. I also have a recollection that on the -- I mean, this is in my report on page 184 that on the 10th of October, they also -- I mean, the SAO SBWS Great Assembly adopts a decision to attach the TO, i.e., the local Serb TO to the -- of the SAO SBWS to the armed forces of SFRY. That's footnote 532.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you'd agree that the development of the district government in the SBWS lagged far behind the development of the district government in the area of the SAO Krajina, right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I haven't specifically looked in that issue. I mean, looking at the dates of -- of certain decisions and so on I would agree with you. I mean, that -- that decisions in SAO SBWS are taken at a later stage than in the SAO Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You testified on Friday I believe it was that you had participated in the drafting of final trial briefs for the Prosecution. Did that include the final trial -- or reviewing and revising final trial briefs for the Prosecution. Did that include the Mrksic final trial brief?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did. And just to avoid misunderstandings, I didn't participate in such activities for the Hadzic trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But you did for the Mrksic case?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And I noticed in the course of your testimony that you often use the verbal expression "between quotation marks" or "in quotation marks." Did you have anything to do with the term SBWS government being referred to in the Prosecution's final trial brief in Mrksic in quotation marks as if to suggest it wasn't a real government?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The use of quotation marks, I mean, I can give you various examples in -- but in relation to the what -- I mean, what we're looking at now, you may have seen -- you may have noticed in the various JNA documents that mention the local authorities prior to the 20th of December, the 1st Military District puts local organs of government or local authorities between quotation marks. My understanding is because this -- these local bodies were not recognised. Whether they are real or not, I mean, that's another matter. I would say this is more for a political expert. After the 20th of November, 1991, I don't remember seeing quotation marks in JNA documents. I use the quotation marks because I want to make it clear to the reader these are not the same bodies as the legal bodies or the legally recognised and the legally established bodies as they existed in the SFRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You know that Radovan Stojicic, aka Badza, arrives in the region of the SBWS in early August, don't you?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It -- it's possible. I don't recall exactly. Early August 1991, yeah, it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you have any awareness at all of the testimony that has been heard in this case.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. As I think I replied on Friday or Thursday, occasionally I look on the Internet just to -- I mean, on Sense Tribunal web site to see which case are on them, and sometimes issues related to this case are being discussed or there are reviews of articles on testimony in this case, but I mean that's not I would say a legal or an authoritative source because it's -- they are paraphrasing the testimony, so that is the furtherest I can be familiar with the testimony in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, we have evidence in this case that Mr. Stojicic shows up in the area of the SBWS in early August, that he convenes a meeting of local TO commanders in Bobota, that he announces that he is the commander of the TO in that area of the SBWS, and that those commanders accept that pronouncement. And he also says that he's there on behalf of the Serbian MUP. Now, listen carefully to this question: Is there any regulation or law from the SFRY or elsewhere suggesting that he was obliged to consult with the prime minister designate of a government that's barely in existence and that has no ministries at all?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe there are several aspects covered in this question. There is no provision in SFRY law that the -- a local -- that a TO is -- is set up in SBWS that doesn't answer to the republican authorities, i.e., the authorities of the Republic of Croatia but instead, based on what Mr. Gosnell just stated, is subordinated to the Ministry of Interior of a neighbouring republic. You know, that is not foreseen by law, so we're in a very grey situation. Now, whether the government is barely in existence and has no ministries at all, what we can say is that again looking at the documents that in the SBWS bodies are set up calling themselves government or authority, and I'm sorry to repeat myself, but that -- until the 20th November 1991, the 1st Military District of the JNA apparently refuses to recognise these bodies because they were' not even identified by name in 1st Military District orders, but after the 20th of November, 1991, the 1st Military District considers these bodies as the relevant authorities and even identifies them as SO, so Serbian District of SBWS bodies of government.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you believe that any reference to SO SBWS implies a reference to the government or can you understand that a reference to SO SBWS could be a reference to a geographic area?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I stated SO SBWS organs or bodies of government, I mean that is the quotation or the text that is being used. Obviously SO SBWS without any additional clarification can be anything. I agree. But I'm specifically talking it -- I mean, it talks about local bodies of government of SO SBWS.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And don't you think that under Article 1 of the Law on All People's Defence - and this Chamber has heard evidence about it, but apparently you're not aware of that - that Serbs at the commune level would consider themselves legally entitled to set up local TOs in order to take up arms against what they perceived as an armed threat from the Croatian side.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, obviously they consider themselves entitled to do so because otherwise they wouldn't have done so. And they were supported -- supported by -- in doing that by Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia as well as the Ministry of Defence and in -- in many cases also -- already initially by the JNA, and later on as we discussed all this becomes regularised and the local Serb TOs become allied forces of the JNA in the operations in Croatia during late summer/fall 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And being, as you say, supported by the Serbian MUP, it's not at all surprising, is it, that Radovan Stojicic could show up on the ground and announce off his own bat, so to speak, or on the basis of the authority of his position in the Serbian MUP that he was the commander of the TO in that area, of the various local TOs in that area?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. And again coming back to my report and the fact I -- I really focussed on -- I mean, I focussed on documents and not on testimony for obvious reasons. I can explain those if needed. I haven't seen a document from the SAO SBWS or from -- from the -- from the prime minister or the president of the government concerning, for example, the removal of Mr. Stojicic or the fact that Mr. Stojicic is showing up and it's unauthorised and that something has to be done about it. Just if you allow me, there is a document from I think January 1992 where Mr. Hadzic allows the 1st Military District to remove --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Excuse me --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, but I would like to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That wasn't my question. You're going into all kinds of matters, and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You may proceed --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I'm very sorry. My hand signal was for the witness, for Mr. Theunens, to stop for a moment. Could you ask the question again, Mr. Gosnell, and I would suggest to Mr. Theunens to try to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yeah, Mr. Theunens, the issue was about whether or not -- and I'll just repeat it because I believe it's clear: It's not surprising that Mr. Radovan Stojicic, given, as you say, that the Serbian MUP was providing support to these local TO groups, and -- announce that he was the commander of these TO units?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, anyone can make any statement. Then we have to see what is the practical effect of this statement, what are the implications.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I want to take you back to page 189 of your report. And this is where you say, and I -- I posed a question about this to you before, and now I come back to it in the context of this discussion. And you say, page 189: "When not participating in combat operations, the local Serb TO in the SAO SBWS is, until at least December 1991, subordinated to the local Serb police under the command of Radovan Stojicic." That's almost right, except the part that you got wrong is that it's not the local Serb police. It's the Serbian MUP, isn't it? That's what you meant to say.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. We discussed this statement. I -- I have difficulties to find the reference -- I mean, I have to admit, to find the reference for the local Serb police because I don't have the same access to the material as I used to have when I was here. So, I mean, if -- if Mr. Gosnell challenges that I have to accept that because I cannot clarify given the material I have in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But when you wrote this report you knew that Mr. Stojicic was affiliated with the SUP of -- with the Serbian MUP; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that but I also remember that there was a clear lack of documents. I mean, there's lot of open sources that mention that, and I was looking for documents to -- to -- to be able to establish the position held by Mr. Stojicic at that time as well as his exact -- I mean, the position in the MUP Serbia and the nature of his relations with the MUP Serbia. And given the lack of footnote there, I haven't been able to -- to establish that and the same applies to the local Serb police. I must have had a document but the footnote isn't there so I cannot -- what I say, I cannot stand by this claim -- by this statement at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And we know that Arkan arrives in the region at around the same time as Mr. Stojicic; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe there's a JNA document that mentions him -- I mean, Arkan in the area of Tenja already in May 1991, so that would be earlier than what you mentioned for Mr. Stojicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, we know at the very at least that Arkan is involved in operations on 1st and 2nd August 1991, correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean, I have no exact recollection but probably it is. I mean, that would have been established from the new documents. In the old documents I don't think I have any document that refers to Arkan's involvement in operations on the 1st and 2nd except -- yeah, I recall now, I think that security organ report in relation to Arkan's alleged or his group blowing up of a Catholic church tower in Erdut around that time-period.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I think that was the Helsinki watch report; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And we have the certificate from Arkan himself describing a wounded soldier in Tenja on the 2nd of August; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And we have the certificate from Arkan indicating that one of his soldiers was wounded in Tenja on the 2nd of August, 1991; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I mean, unless this is a memory test, it would be helpful for me to see the actual document otherwise I can just say, yeah, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, we discussed them on Friday, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And we know that the JNA identified the training centre in Erdut, as you said, identified the training centre in Erdut as a training facility of the Croatian TO prior to the conflict; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. But I think the wording there is -- could be misunderstood. There was in Erdut a facility prior to the war which, according to documents we saw, was used by I think Croatian Ministry of Interior. It may have been also been Republic of Croatia TO but that is prior to the war. But there is no handover from the Croats to the local Serbs or what.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I fully understand that there are no documents about that, but what I'm asking you -- what I propose to ask you is this: Do you think given that the JNA is on the ground in Erdut in force on the 1st of August, and Badza is on the ground in early August, do you think either the JNA or Badza needs to go to Goran Hadzic and ask him for permission as to the use of that TO training centre?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer that question, Your Honours. All I can say is that based on JNA 1st Military District documents -- as I mentioned earlier, the 1st Military District doesn't recognise the local SAO or SO SBWS authorities; on the other hand, security organs report of the 1st Military District between October 1991 and, say, January 1992, mention, for example, that Arkan has close relations with -- with local Serb authorities, but how the centre in Erdut became a training centre for Arkan and then for the local Serb -- for the local SAO SBWS TO, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, you seem very comfortable drawing other types of inferences. Why can't you draw an inference in this case that the training centre was handed over to Arkan either by the JNA directly or by Badza?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Isn't that asked and answered, Mr. Gosnell?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well I put the question a bit more forcefully and a bit more leadingly, Mr. President, but I take your point. I will move on if it's your wish. Shall I move on? Thank you, Mr. President. Could we have 05998, which is Defence tab 492.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And, Mr. Theunens, what I'd like to do now is to take you through a number of documents chronologically that show what is going on in the TO at this time-period in this area, or at least I hope they will show that. Now, this is dated the 30th of September, 1991. It's from the command of the 12th Corps, Major-General Mladen Bratic, and he is talking about the formation of a tactical group to unify the command of blocking Vukovar from the north, and he appoints a commander and the staff of this TG, and then it says: "The following units and commands will be subordinated to the TG commander." Starts with a JNA unit. And then it says: "Volunteer TO detachment from Valjevo," so that's Serbia, "TO company from Borovo Selo, TO company from Brsadin." Now this indicates, doesn't it, that the JNA is subordinating TO units -- local TO units in the area; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Local Serb TO units.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We would tender that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit D40. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 6000, which is Defence tab 390.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This again is from the command of the 12th Corps. This time signed by the Chief of Staff, Colonel Srboljub Trajkovic. The date is the 1st of October, 1991, and the subject is permits for movement in the combat zone. It says: "Attached please find the permits for the movement in the combat zone. Permits to be issued to every officer by name for those who need to move in the combat zone in order to supply units, deliver goods, and evacuation. Individuals without permit attached cannot move during the night neither cross the bridge over the Danube by Bogojevo without this permit." First of all, does this reflect that the JNA is controlling movement in the area?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. But just to be precise, I mean, the combat zone, and this is delineated by the -- the limits of the various zones of responsibility of the units. But it's -- it makes sense, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And given that Bogojevo bridge is mentioned, wouldn't you agree that it seems that the zone of responsibility goes right up to the Bogojevo bridge in the depth of the territory?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if we look at the list of addressees, no mention there at all, is there, of a TO SBWS headquarters, General Staff, HQ, anything of that kind; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can't see the -- I would like to see the list of addressees. I think it's at the bottom, the left bottom corner of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yes. If we could scroll down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah. Oops. Yes, according to the handwritten additions, it is only sent to subordinate units of the 12th Corps, JNA units.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We would tender that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit D41. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 00444, please. And that's Prosecution tab 123.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, this is from the SFRY Official Gazette. The date is the 18th of October but it refers to a proclamation dated the 1st of October, 1991. It says: "According to the Article 316 of the SFRY Constitution and Article 6 of the Law on All People's Defence ... at the session held on ...," and then there appears to be a typo if you see there, "the 1st of November 1991, the SFRY Presidency estimating current political-safety situation in the country proclaimed existence of imminent war danger in SFRY number 190, Belgrade, 1 October, 1991." Now, sir, just a very brief correction: In your report you indicate that this proclamation of 3rd. Do we -- can we agree that it's actually the 1st of October, 1991?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please tell me on which page my report is this discussed, because I think there I refer also to a JNA document which uses the 3rd. So I agree with you that it should be the 1st, but maybe we should explain why I apparently erroneously wrote it was the 3rd.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That's page 135 of your report.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. Yeah, I think -- I mean, if you pointed out -- I think it's also helpful to point out footnote 374 which states that the decision or the -- the establishment of the state of imminent threat of war by the SFRY Presidency is on the 1st of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: All right. So the footnote is correct and it's just the text that is wrong; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we should have -- look at all the references, because it wouldn't -- I mean, why I would write the 3rd if I write in the footnote it's the 1st, so because there are other documents. I think maybe it's not in the cut and paste or in the amalgamated report, but there is a follow-up document by I think organ for morale at the SSNO or the General Staff of the JNA to explain to the JNA personnel the implications of this declaration by the SFRY Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I don't why you would do that. But you've got the document there quite clearly in front of you. The date of the proclamation is 1st of October, 1991; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's in the footnote. 374.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I would tender this document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, just to remain consistent with the policy we adopted on Friday. This is one of the documents that will be part of the package we will be including. It's one of the documents in the footnotes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. It will be admitted with the package. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: What's the consequence of this proclamation in your view, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I haven't seen any specific documents to that effect. Just from the context one would say that, okay, it will -- it can be used to declare additional mobilisations as well deployment of forces but I haven't seen any specific documents except, as I mentioned, there is this document from the JNA or General Staff or SSNO administration for moral guidance on the practical implications, mainly for morale of the troops. But that's all I have seen and I thought this document was included in the report but I cannot locate it as of now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I should have been more precise in my question. What is your view of the legal consequence of this proclamation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is outside the scope of my expertise, Your Honours. I haven't looked into that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Outside of the scope of your expertise and yet you rely at length in your report on the Law on All People's Defence, the SFRY constitution, and many other SFRY laws. Are you saying that you included material that's not within the scope of your expertise?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, Your Honours, that my answer was clear. What -- I will try to clarify my answer, then. I haven't -- I'm not aware of any specific documents from after the 1st of October, 1991, explaining what the legal implications are of the -- the mentioned proclamation by the SFRY Presidency. I don't recall seeing such documents. If you would show me such documents then maybe I can be helpful to you and try to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: In your view as a matter of law, does it have any impact on the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as we discussed earlier, it would imply the formal establishment of the Supreme Command as well as the staff of the Supreme Command. However, as we discussed during my examination, the Supreme Command was already in existence de facto prior to the 1st of October, 1991, and the same applies to the staff of the Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, now I'm very confused because I thought that the Supreme Command was in existence prior to this date de jure, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's maybe a matter of defining de jure and de facto. When I say de facto, I mean that the Supreme Command is issuing decisions or is -- I will correct that is -- is quoted I mean, the -- the term "Supreme Command" is used in JNA documents and SFRY armed forces documents. The same applies to the staff of the Supreme Command even prior to 1st of October. That's why I used de facto because it's only on the 1st of October that the SFRY Presidency, 1st of October, 1991, that the SFRY Presidency proclaims the existence of an imminent threat of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So is it your testimony that de jure there is no Supreme Command of the SFRY prior to the 1st of August, 1991?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have answered the question. I have stated that -- I have stated a number of -- of -- of for that the bodies, i.e., called Supreme Command or identified as Supreme Command is according to the documents I reviewed already existing prior to 1st of October, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I want to be very precise about your view on this, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Is it in existence de jure prior to that date or not?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe I have answered the question to the best of my abilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Does that mean you don't know?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not a question -- sorry. It's not a question of knowing or not knowing, but I'm not going to make a statement on issues like de jure when I haven't looked into that matter. I'm not a political analyst. I haven't looked at constitutional issues in the SFRY beyond the level that is required to understand the functioning of the JNA during summer and fall 1991, and I believe that the answer I have given to the question so far, and I think I repeated myself three times, is the best I can do in order to assist you in relation to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 060055, please -- excuse me, let me restate that number: 06005, Defence tab 395.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This is a regular combat report from the 12th Corps Command signed by Major-General Mladen Bratic, dated 4 October 1991. The location of the report seems to be village of Dalj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: If we go to page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if we can just look at the last sentence of (d) and (e) there on the page: "2/18 pmtbr remained in the region of village Bogojevo and on 5 October will be redeployed in the region of Klisa. The 12th pmbr with part of its forces attacked the axis village Silas village, Markusica village, Sodolovci, where they provided assistance to the units of TO in repelling the attack ..." Now can you tell from the way that that reference is formulated that that is local TO or would you not be able to say that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you look at the document in isolation, one would not be able to answer the question. But looking at the overall context, by that time by the 1st October it would be highly unlikely that the JNA would be supporting units of the TO of the Republic of Croatia. So, again, looking at the context, this has to be local Serb TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I would tender that document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit D42. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 6008, which is Defence tab 398.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, this doesn't specifically concern TO, but there are one or two issues I would like your assistance on, and we're proceeding in chronological order which is why I put the document to you. It's a command report, regular command report of the 12th Corps dated the 5th of October, 1991, again signed by Major Bratic -- or General Bratic: "During the day, the members of the armed formations of the Republic of Croatia carried out a stiff defence in the town of Vukovar. Despite our call, they did not agree to surrender." Do you know whether there were periodic calls to surrender by the JNA to the Croatian forces in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I mean, this is one example. I'm not fully familiar with the time of the -- the timings of other examples but there is also quite highly publicised I wouldn't call it effort but attempt by Mr. Seselj when he visits Vukovar - I think this is early November or in October 1991 - and he is allowed to drive around with a vehicle and he has a megaphone where he calls the "Ustashas" to surrender. When I say he is allowed, he is allowed by the JNA to drive around or to move around in a vehicle with a megaphone. And this is when he is visiting OG South I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you know whether there were calls by the JNA itself or are you suggesting Seselj was a part of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I answered the question. So I'm -- this is one example. I belive that there were also calls -- other calls by the JNA, and I mentioned in addition Seselj because that's also an example of a call to the Croats to surrender.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Going over to page 2, I won't quote the passages but I'm interested in subparagraphs (f) and (g). And it's talking about movements of units in the first case between the village of Dalj and the village of Trpinja, and then the village of Rogojevo to the village of Klisa? Now, can I ask you as relying on your military expertise, is it normal that there are movements of forces of this nature within the zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, this is normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And what kind of, if any, would -- security measures would be implied by those types of movements?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I fully understand the question. What do you mean what kind of security measures would be taken or what kind of measures would be made to secure, protective measures or -- to protect the movements?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, the movements would be -- would be -- ideally they would be conducted at night. I'm just giving a generic answer now, but movements to be conducted at night to avoid detection from the air which is obviously not an issue in Eastern Slavonia in 1991 because there is no Croatian air force. You would use military police to control crossings -- I mean, to avoid interference -- or road junctions to avoid interference with other traffic. Ideally, you would also send patrols before the convoys as well as -- in potentially vulnerable locations to avoid that there are attempts by infiltrated enemy forces to threaten the convoy, because when moving, of course, units are more vulnerable than when being static. I mean, you would try to take all necessary measures to avoid like, for example, ambushes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We would tender this document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit D43. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have P1686, please, Prosecution tab 149.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This is another report of the 12th Corps dated I believe the 8th of October 1991, although I cannot see that on the English version. But I'm interested in one specific passage from this document. If we could turn to page 3, first full paragraph: "Direct engagement of people in combat operations has led to the deaths and wounding of some soldiers ..." What do you think is meant by the expression "direct engagement of people in combat operations"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It -- it means that JNA person -- or, yeah, JNA or subordinate personnel is involved in combat operations and those can consist of -- I mean, depending on the nature of troops, but if it's infantry, I mean, this can include exchanges of fire with opposing forces or maybe they are exposed to shelling by the opposing forces. It could be -- I mean, it doesn't explain exactly what kind of operations they are conducting, whether it's offensive or defensive operations, but all of these operations would include exchanges of fire of various nature. It can be direct fire, can be indirect fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: All right. And let's go to the next page: "Security situation in units and in the territory ... on the whole, the system of security and /illegible/ in the zone of combat operations of the 12th Corps is not functioning as it should. The newly established organs of authority haven't gained control over the security situation in the field to the necessary extent and there are different views and opinions among them on how to resolve problems while a few local staffs function independently. A large number of former agents of the State Security Service of the Republic of Croatia, some of whom have radio stations, use those to report on positions and conditions in our units to the enemy, which also contributes to the infiltration of reconnaissance and sabotage groups? Now, first question: Do you agree that it seems that General Bratic, who is the author of this report, seems to be very preoccupied with infiltration and sabotage in his zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. And I think it's important to know that the 12th Corps is operating in an area where obviously there are a number of municipalities with a Serb majority but there is also municipalities with a Croatian majority, and obviously he has doubts about the allegiance of these Croats, and according to the information he believes that they are still in contact with the Croatian authorities and maybe gathering information, transmitting that information, as well as also maybe assisting or -- yeah, assisting in Croatian infiltration, enemy infiltration in the zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And the second sentence there referring to the newly established organs, do you agree with me that that's probably a reference to local TO staffs?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would -- I -- and I mean, I haven't discussed it in the report, this document, the amalgamated report, obviously, because it's a new document, but I discuss it in the report that was submitted in October. My conclusion was that it was bodies of the SO SAO SBWS because if it was TO, I mean, to answer your question, he would have referred to local Serb TO or to local TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I assumed you were going to say that, Mr. Theunens and that's why I put the question to you, but take a look at the last part of the sentence. On the one hand in the first part of the sentence you see a reference to "newly established organs not having gained control over the security situation," and then in the last part of the sentence you see him saying: "While a few local staffs function independently." Now, wouldn't you agree that that second reference, that express reference to local staffs implies that the earlier reference is also to local staffs? Is the transcript okay, or are --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It -- it is possible -- I would agree with you that if there's a reference to a local staff it would be TO, but we know that there is also groups like Arkan operating. And again, we cannot really draw a conclusion on the staffs because Bratic doesn't identify the nature of these staffs, so what I would do then, again, from an analytical point of view or a methodological point of view is to try to look at other documents in order to better understand the context and then hopefully be in a better position to draw a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Isn't Arkan if he is subordinated to the armed forces a member of the TO by definition?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In theory, yes, but in practice the volume of reports from the 1st Military District - and again we have been going over them quite a few times already - show that there are difficulties with the status of Arkan and his relations with the JNA. There are for sure orders that he is subordinated to the JNA at specific moments in time and closely co-operating. There are also documents in the latter group. I see, for example, reports of the security organs of 1st Military District where his relations with the JNA are not entirely clear let alone his subordination at that specific moment in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Isn't that precisely why this document would say a few local staffs function independently?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, Your Honours, it's possible. I don't dispute that. It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 06077, please, which is Defence tab 407.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This is a 12th Corps Command order dated the 11th of October, 1991.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we have another document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Is that 6077? May I just have one moment, Your Honour. Well, again my handwriting has failed me. It's 65 ter 6017. Now if we can just go to page 3 of this document which again is a 12th Corps Command order dated the 11th of October, 1991, village of Dalj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Item 8 says: "36th mbr," and then there's an expansion unknown but there is a reference to TO, "shall establish full control over the territory of Baranja in co-operation with Baranja TO units." Would you agree again this is an example of local TO units being subordinated to the JNA.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, indeed the Baranja TO units are units of the local Serb TOs so SAO SBWS. Now, again, in co-operation doesn't mean that the Baranja TO would be subordinated to the 36th Mechanised Brigade. However, since this -- the TO Baranja is mentioned in the document of the 12th Corps, in this context it implies that indeed these Baranja TO units are subordinated to the 12th Corps at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Go to page 5. It says: "Various individuals and groups acting independently have started appearing in areas of combat looting and terrorising the population and similar. Regiment brigade commands are required to get in touch with such groups and individuals in their respective areas of responsibility, place them under their command, and control their behaviour, demanding them to stick to the same laws obeyed by the JNA in the [sic] area. Otherwise, take energetic steps to prevent their independent actions and behaviour." Now that speaks for itself, but the question I have for you is would you agree that the duty to subordinate - you know what I mean by that, and I know you don't like the term, but the concept is agreed between us - the duty to subordinate extends to groups showing up in the territory and looting civilians? Looting civilian homes, for example.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, that is correct, to subordinate them or remove them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And are they subject to military jurisdiction as military persons?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If -- if they accepted to be subordinated, then obviously they would become a member of the armed forces and therefore be subjected to military discipline and military justice system. The question, of course, is what if -- what would happen if they refused to be subordinated and no measures were taken or no successful measures were taken to remove them. I mean, I'm not aware of any - we discussed it during the examination - of any investigations by the military prosecutors in SFRY and in FRY in 1991, 1992, 1993 concerning the activities of volunteers, but it was more toward the civilian judicial instances who at a rather late stage, and I think I quoted from a Human Rights Watch report referring to investigation and trial proceedings or attempts for trial proceedings against members of the volunteer group known as Yellow Wasps and their alleged crimes committed in Zvornik in April 1991, Zvornik in Bosnia-Herzegovina. So, yeah, I mean if they accepted to be subordinated, then obviously they would be members of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Are you telling me that whether or not they are subject to military justice depends on whether or not they have agreed to be subordinated? It's their choice?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the way you formulate the question, you -- you make subordination seem as -- as -- as an issue of choice. When you look at this document in isolation, but again we can look at it in the context of others and they say similar things. The JNA leaves room open for consultation with these groups to, i.e., that the commander asks them, well, or tells them: You will be subordinated and then you will act in accordance with the rules and regulations or you will be removed. What I mentioned in the second part of my answer to the previous question is -- is a third option: What happens with groups who refuse to be subordinate but who remain in the area. I have heard, but I haven't seen any documents about it, but I have heard while working here that, for example, the Guard Motorised Brigade used its military police to remove such groups manu militari, i.e., to use military force to kick such groups who refused to be subordinated to the JNA out. Without going repeating too much what I have said already before, I think from the documents it's clear that groups like Arkan, given their relations or their special relations with authorities of the Republic of Serbia, MUP, and MOD, and also with the local Serb authorities, they seem to have been treated in a different manner by the 12th Corps, in particular after General Bratic was killed in action and General Biorcevic takes over. Now, basically Biorcevic praises Arkan for his activities and -- okay, in that situation we see that at times from the documents on combat operations that Arkan and his group are subordinated to the JNA, but again security organs of the 1st Military District also provide other information.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We're going to come to a couple of documents later but the difficulty I have with your answer is that I thought we had discussed carefully the Law on All People's Defence, and my understanding was that if someone arrives in a zone of responsibility and takes up arms in defence of the country, they are deemed to be a part of the Territorial Defence. And in turn under the SFRY constitution, if you're a part of the Territorial Defence, you're part of the armed forces. So what I understand, and I -- this is -- this is where I want your comment: What I understand is the mere fact of showing up in the area, whether or not you abide by the instructions of the local JNA commander, you are a military person and therefore subject to military justice. Isn't that the way it is?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. It is not. And I mean, I can elaborate again but I will partially repeat what I have been testifying over the past days so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: If that's your position, Mr. Theunens, that's all right as an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yes. I would tender this document, please, 6-0.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit D44. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 00422, please, Prosecution tab 117.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now we've looked at this document -- at paragraph 1 of this document already. I don't want to go back to paragraph 1 but I do want to go down to paragraph 5, and this is a 1st Military District Command order, 15th of October, 1991: "Form the Military District command for the AO of Slavonia, Western Srem, and Baranja with the centre in Dalj, organise the military sections in Beli Manastir and Ilok upon its liberation." Now, first of all, just as a matter of nomenclature, would you agree with me that that reference to the AO of Slavonia, Western Srem, and Baranja, that's a geographic reference, correct? There is no implication that this miliary district command is going to be connected to the district government is there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. It's for the geographic area. I was just comparing with the B/C/S because the word "district," I mean, it's -- the B/C/S exactly "oku [phoen]." It's not the same as "ooblast." So it's the territorial structure, not an operational structure like the 1st Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And what does it mean that the a military district command is being set up? Why is that being done, if I could ask for your assistance?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is connected to issue of establishing town commands; i.e., according to the 1st Military District there are no functioning or recognised civilian authorities and this is why the JNA has to take care of that. And in this document, I have referred to in my testimony a few times to this order by General Panic of 15th October 1991, he highlights these problems. And I think it is also in this document or a follow-up document of the 16th November that he refers to attempts of local bodies of authority without explicitly identifying them but attempts to interfere in -- in the situation and Panic orders his subordinate commanders to prevent such attempts.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I believe this is part of the package so I'll say no more about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's look at one of those attempts that you're referring to, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: L12, Defence tab 167, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now this is a decision on the organisation and activity of the Territorial Defence and Civilian Protection apparently passed by the SBWS Assembly, Great National Assembly. And the date appears to be the 17th of October.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So that's two days after the document we just looked at. Now --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, could I please see the bottom of the document, because I think the bottom explains when the decision has been taken or when it has been published. Or maybe the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We could go to page 7 of the English.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now if we could go back to page 2 of the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if we could look at Article 3: "The commander of the Territorial Defence of the Serbian district and commanders of the Territorial Defence of settlements, within the rights and duties determined by this decision, shall organise and prepare the Territorial Defence, control it, and ensure its unified organisation, preparation, and action." Now, at this point, Mr. Theunens, as you know, the SFRY Presidency has declared an imminent state of war. Can I ask you whether it's your view whether Article 3 interferes with the JNA's chain of command -- or interrupts the JNA's chain of command over local TO units?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- Your Honours, I would prefer to word it differently because, I mean, I don't see a conflict or an inconsistency between Article 3 on one hand and SFRY armed forces doctrine on the other hand, whereby I referred for the doctrine to the 1982 All People's Defence law so that the two are consistent.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I would agree with you that they are consistent and I appreciate that comment. Would you agree with me that what is reflected in Article 3 is purely the managerial function in respect of TOs and does not reflect a command and control function, either in war time or in peacetime?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I agree with -- with your proposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would tender that document -- oh, it's tendered, I'm sorry. L12. Would that be a convenient moment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Very convenient, Mr. Gosnell. Mr. Theunens, first break. We'll come back at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You'll be escorted out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Let's have a look at the planning. Mr. Gosnell, how long do you think you'll have?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: It's a bit hard to say, Mr. President. I really had hoped to finish today. There have been some extremely long answers. You'll notice that I have not been interrupting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. So you hope to finish today but not before the end of the hearing. Is that more or less what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I would be very surprised if I -- if I was able to. Of course, nothing is impossible in this world.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: How about your re-direct, Mr. Demirdjian?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It will be, so far, about 15, 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So we're looking at tomorrow morning continuing Mr. Theunens testimony?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I suspect. Depending on when the Defence finishes their cross-examination, probably the first session, yeah, roughly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Could we have 65 ter 460, which is Prosecution tab 128.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And this is a -- an order or document from General Panic, commander of the 1st Military District, dated the 19th of October, 1991. If we can just cast our eyes over the addressees on page 1. We see that it's addressed to the Vojvodina Provincial Territorial Defence HQ. No reference here to any Provincial Territorial Defence HQ of SBWS, is there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours. And if you want I can -- I can provide an explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, what's your explanation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mean it basically comes back to the point I expressed earlier, that is that basically two points: First of all, Panic doesn't, as commander of the 1st Military District, doesn't recognise the local Serb TO as a -- as an established TO structure; and, on the other hand, units of the local Serb TO, when they're operating under JNA command, well, it's sufficient for Panic to issue his orders to the -- to the units of the JNA because he knows that based on the principles of command and control they will -- I mean, the subordinate units will inform the subordinate local Serb TO units of the instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Page 2, top of page : "Terrorist operations in the rear of our units which would be carried out by groups of the Black Shirts that have been left behind or infiltrated are to be expected." And then there is an allegation by General Panic that the Medecins Sans Frontieres convoy has basically been used as a cover for smuggling weapons into Vukovar. Do you go that that's what he's saying?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mean, to be precise he talks about the arrival of fresh troops and combat equipment but not into Vukovar but to Vinkovci and to Nustar. So I'm reading it as you speak, so I'm trying to find the passage you are referring to, but maybe you can help me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, that's a fair distinction, yes. The convoy appears to have been used as some kind of a distraction, would you agree, to bring supplies to Vinkovci and Nustar, right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't go that far. You know, maybe it -- they used this kind of -- as a deception or what, but you would have to look at the documents from the Croatian side in order to -- to find out more about this. We see that Panic uses the expression "synchronized" but I cannot establish what he -- I mean, I know what synchronises means. It's -- there's a coincidence or co-ordination in time, but what the motives for that are I don't think we can establish that from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I'm not really interested in establishing the facts one or the other. What I am interested in is General Panic's perception of the situation, and wouldn't you agree that he seems to be very concerned about -- well, as he says there in the first sentence, "groups that have been left behind or infiltrated"; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct and that corresponds with the operational situation as I have also seen it mentioned or discussed by the JNA in the area at that moment in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, if we go over to page 3, item 4: "In order to prevent looting, the abuse of citizens, and murder, even that of captives, all armed persons and groups which are not in the JNA and TO composition, Chetniks, et cetera, are to be disarmed and detained, and the leaders incarcerated and legal measures taken against them." Now this is germane to the answer that you gave just before the break in which you were expressing, if I can put it pithily, I think you were suggesting that these volunteer formations are subject to military justice if they're only acting badly, but if they're acting very very badly they're not subject to military justice. Now looking at this paragraph, isn't Panic saying even if they're acting very very badly, they're under military jurisdiction, military justice jurisdiction?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, maybe Mr. Gosnell can point me to the -- or can cite from my testimony, but I don't remember using the kind of expressions he is using now. I don't think you're even paraphrasing my previous testimony. What I tried to explain was the situation as I have seen it from the documents; i.e., whether or not these members of volunteer groups and local Serb TO were subordinated to the TO -- to the JNA at the time of the crimes or not. The order by Panic is not necessarily a reflection of the implementation of the system of military justice. What it is is that Panic, as commander of the 1st Military District, is, again, because there are several documents, ordering his subordinate commanders to implement the principles of command and control, i.e., to ensure at all times single and unified command and control over all the forces in their zone of responsibility, and obviously if members of these forces commit crimes, well, to make measures against them in order to prevent further crimes from being committed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Not just any measures, take legal measures against them; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And then we are in the area of -- of the 1988 instructions on the implementation of the laws of war by the SFRY armed forces, and again without referring to the specific articles this implies that -- I mean, based on the level of authority, that commanders, any -- actually any officer who sees a crime, informs the appropriate organs so that it can be investigated, and then we know that military police and security organs have specific duties and even rights and that, for example, security organs and then for sure military police can arrest or detain --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- alleged perpetrators of crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens I put it to you that the duty to report a crime is irrelevant here. The issue here is Article 1 of the Law on Military Courts and the jurisdiction over what is described there as military persons. And what I'm putting to you is that even these individuals who are acting very, very badly, are considered military persons and within the jurisdiction of military justice; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, because, I mean, you have -- you have read out paragraph 4. I think it's very clear. It states in the second line: "All armed persons and groups --" oh, yeah, sorry, I touched the screen, "-- which are not in the JNA ..." That is the whole issue and that is the whole problem in fall 1991; that is - and I'm sorry to repeat it again - but we have various groups, party affiliated or supported by the Ministry of Interior or the MOD of Serbia, who appear. Some of them are very well organised and very well equipped like Arkan's Tigers. And even if Panic doesn't explicitly refer to the Arkan Tigers in his paragraph 4, but he talk about all armed persons in groups which are not in the JNA and the TO. And again from the context, I conclude from that that he is referring to groups like Arkan, the -- the Dusan Silni, even -- and if there would be -- he talks about Chetniks even though we know that in OG South, for example, a detachment of volunteers affiliated with the SRS are, I mean, Leva Supoderica, are identified as Seselj TO detachments in one order and as TO detachment Leva Supoderica in another order.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, if they are not deemed or considered to be military persons within Article 1 of the Law on Military Courts, then what is the basis for General Panic saying that legal measures be taken against them?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would say irrespective of your status whether you're civilian or military, if you engage in looting or the abuse of citizens and if you engage in murder, even captives, in an area where according to the 1st Military District there is no recognised civilian authority, then it's up to the military to take measures. And if you want, I can explain you why it makes sense that Panic repeatedly issues such instructions during fall 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, are you saying that he therefore falls into the other head of jurisdiction in Article 1 of the Law on Military Courts. And just for your assistance, Mr. Theunens, this is at page 103 of your report, and the other head of jurisdiction is it says criminal acts committed by military persons and by other persons when such criminal acts are related to the national defence. So you -- and you have that provision in front of you?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Would it be your position that these volunteer groups which are declining to be subordinated fall into the other head of jurisdiction under Article 1?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, perhaps they do. But I mean, I also wish to draw the Court's attention that Panic doesn't refer to the Law on Military Courts and the Law on Military Prosecutors. He doesn't need that. He looks at as a commander who is responsible for the situation in his zone of responsibility and irrespective obviously of the legal prohibitions in relation to commission of crimes he is also concerned by the implications for his forces of such behaviour taking place in his zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We're going back to back to this issue but that's as far as I can take it with this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Are you, Mr. Gosnell?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: For the umpteenth time?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I mean, the witness has explained his position and answered your questions at least three or four times and his answer is always the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I understand. But I'll have two documents later that are very precise on this point and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Let's give it a go.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- what I propose. But I'm not going to do that now. I'm just putting a bookmark into the issue, Mr. President. Could I tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It's part of the package, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Could we have 496, please, Prosecution tab 140.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now this is -- as it comes up on the screen, I'll say what it is for the record. It's an OG South command decision signed by Mile Mrksic dated the 29th of October, 1991. And down under units tasks, we see a reference to the detachment Leva Supoderica and the detachment Petrova Gora. Are those both local TO units from the area of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, these are local Serb TO units which have been established by the local Serbs in the course of summer/fall 1991 and some -- I mean, at least Leva Supoderica involves also volunteers from Serbia which would be irregular when compared with the legal framework or the doctrinal framework that organised or regulated the republican TOs as -- as is for example explained in 1982 All People's Defence law.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And yet they're being subordinated here by Mrksic; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now if we go over to page 2, item 3. Again, we see TO units Negoslavci and Sotin from the current area of combat deployment. Again, does that reflect subordination of local TO Serb units to the OG South?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. Local Serb TO units just to avoid confusion. And this is discussed also on page 457 of my report, the amalgamated report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I would tender this document if it's not part of the package. I'll say no more. Thank you. Could we have 6022, please. Defence tab 404.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, sir, I understand that your thesis is that the town commands of the JNA are exercising civilian authority up until the 20th of November. But then you say that after the order of the 20th of November, which we're coming to, they adopt an advisory role vis-a-vis the civilian authorities. Does that correctly summarise your position?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours. And just for clarity of the record, 20th of November, 1991, and the order is to 2436-1 from the 1st Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you for that. And if we look at paragraph 1 of this document, would you agree that that reflects what you've just said about the position prior to the 20th of November, 1991?
