utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just -- I mean, clarifying. It's a new document. It became available in September/October. Yes, I mean, it corresponds with -- it's consistent with the pattern or the role of the town commander had described in the amalgamated report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I tender this document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honours. This document was already admitted and marked on 10th January 2013 through Witness Nielsen. Thank you. Exhibit P365. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Could we have 00586, please, which is Prosecution tab 167.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now this is from the 1st Military District Command dated the 16th of November, 1991. Again, we see the listing of addressees and again we see no reference to any SBWS TO but we do see a reference to the Vojvodina provincial TO staff. Now I just want to take you down, if I may, to point 1: "Apply the same treatment to the attached and the resubordinated units of the JNA, the TO, and the volunteer compositions, if they are put under the command of the JNA units ...," this is the part I'd like you to focus on, Mr. Theunens, the last bit, "... regardless of whether they are engaged in the carrying out of combat tasks, the control of the territory, or the establishment of military authority." Now, would you agree that all three of those functions are within the scope of the JNA's activities, first of all?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, they fall within the scope of JNA's activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And TOs and/or what is referred here to as volunteer compositions can be used for any of those JNA activities; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is indeed what the paragraph states, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can we go now to page 2, please, and item 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And there's some military language here that I found a bit obscure and I was hoping you could help us. "The military authority and the town commands" -- Well, let me go back to the beginning of item 2: "Immediately start establishing the military authority and the town commands in liberated territory and settlements." Now, is this the 16th of November. Do you think that it's likely that General Panic, on the one hand is arguing or is declaring -- start establishing military authority and town commands in the liberated territory on the 16th, and that then on the 20th he is saying, No need to do that. Just provide assistance to the local authorities?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure of the way you put it, and I don't want to criticise you but the way you put is not an accurate reflection of the documents that are included in my -- even in the amalgamated report where I only had part of the documents available, and I would like to refer to page 491. It's already -- I mean, we discussed it this morning. Already on the 15th of October General Panic issues orders to establish town commands and to prevent or not to permit the local organs of authority to interfere and so on and so on. We discuss that. We see that the military -- excuse me, OG South on the 9th of November informs already the 1st Military District about the establishment of town commands in certain locations. The fact that Panic comes back to this on the 16th of November, given the context, in my view highlights that there are difficulties with the establishment of military authority and that maybe in some of his subordinate units, they are not as diligent or as effective as OG South to establish town commands in the various towns and -- and areas located in the zone of responsibility. And this is why he reiterates his orders. Now, from a military point of view, on the 16th of November, Panic cannot know that Vukovar falls on the 18th, and he can even less well know what is going to happen on the 20th. So I don't think it is -- I mean, again from a methodological point of view relevant to question an order of the 16th of November by referring to an order of 20th November because he doesn't know on the 16th what's going to happen on the 20th.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So it your position that the hand-over of authority to civilian authorities on the 20th of November is related to the fall of Vukovar. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would just to correct it is a gradual hand-over. It's not from -- from moment A or moment B that the situation totally changes because criteria are established and we get these instructions from the SSNO 5881 and 5883 of 25th of November and, I think, 6th of December, 1991, but to -- sorry, to answer the question: The fall of Vukovar is a key event because, again - and that is with hindsight - we know that on the 23rd November a major cease-fire agreement is agreed in Geneva and this is not something that is decided on the 23rd. It's reasonable to assume that once Vukovar falls -- okay, there is a surrender on the 18 and then the city is entirely under JNA control maybe except for some resistance pockets by the 20th, and we have the evacuation of the hospital and so on. It is clear that this means the end of offensive combat operations by the JNA in SBWS.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now the terminology that I was hoping you could assist us with is the next sentences. "The military authority and the town commands in the depth of the zone of JNA regiment brigade in contact are established by the units of the first echelon and by the autonomous province of Vojvodina TO staffs in the depth according to the second echelon and in the regions of the deployment of the reserve. The lowest levels of the establishment of the town commands are the companies." Can you explain what that means in layman's terms, please?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it means that -- I mean, it would be easier would be to use a map and to see where the line -- the contact line, i.e., the confrontation line between the JNA on one hand and the Croatian forces on the other hand is located, and then obviously in the first line I would say the main units -- trying to look how it was expressed here, but the units of the first echelon are not only deployed but are being used. Of course, there is a whole depth in, as I mentioned also in earlier days, where for example logistical units are deployed, communication units and so on, because there's no interest in putting them on the front line. On the contrary, it would expose them because they -- they are not organised to defend themselves, so the same applies to units of second and third echelon, and then the use of first echelon, second, and third echelon is a concept the SFRY armed forces doctrine. But Panic tries to say that these -- the military control should not only be established close to the front line but all over the zone of responsibility using the respective units that are deployed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens, for that explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we tender this -- no we can't tender it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have D10, please, Prosecution tab 131.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now this is describing -- it's an order from the 9th Corps Command by General Major Vukovic, and it concerns Bosnia to be clear. But the reason why I am showing you this document comes back to our issue of jurisdiction over TO units. And it says here at item 2: "From their own composition and from the composition of the subordinated TO units and other armed compositions of the city command in the municipality centres, the commands of the JNA units at the level of a regiment-brigade in their AOR and the zone where the combat activities are being carried out will form platoons for the protection of the citizens and the property and in the local communities they will form sections." So is that a typical task that should be carried out by a town command?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is -- I mean, yeah, it falls within the tasks of a town command. But obviously we see a distinction or difference between what is happening in the zone of responsibility of the 9th corps, i.e., in northern -- or in Dalmatia on the one hand and the zone of responsibility of, for example, OG South or the 1st Military District on the other hand because the documents of OG South only mention Guards Motorised Brigade personnel being used to form the town command. There is no further specification as to the use of TO like it is done by the 9th Corps in tasks of the town command.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, as a matter of doctrine and practice, wouldn't JNA commanders who are setting up town commands have the same understanding of the scope of their activities and responsibilities?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But they can decide themselves on which forces to use for -- for what task.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now if we just go over to page 2, item 4: "Criminal charges are to be filed through the closest command of the JNA units in line with the provisions of the penal code for all persons for whom justified suspicions exists that they committed a criminal act. "Perpetrators of the crimes from the jurisdiction of the military court are to be arrested and through the police of commands of the regiments-brigades of the JNA are to be escorted to the military police in Knin." So apparently I made a mistake. It's actually not Bosnia, it's apparently the --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, it's Dalmatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yes. Can you tell us what the basis for this jurisdiction is that's being asserted by this commander?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be useful to look again at the beginning of the document whether there's a reference to an order of a higher echelon or reference to a doctrinal document or maybe even as we discussed earlier the Law on Military Courts or Law on Military Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, just for your assistance on that there isn't.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. If there's not, there's not. And -- I mean, he is applying the doctrine. This includes also as I mentioned earlier the 1988 SFRY armed -- sorry, regulations on the application of the laws of war by the SFRY armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 00577, Prosecution tab 163.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This is dated the 14th of November, 1991. It's from the OG South Command. Which should be Colonel Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And it's just items 4 and 5 that I'm interested in. We see there he is saying: "Limit all unnecessary movement in the regions of deployment while fully implementing the signs of identification and FOM passes." Is that freedom of movement passes?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume it is. I mean, unless the B/C/S uses -- is a different wording but then FOM is usually the acronym for freedom of movement, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: It says: "Establish full control over the movement in and out of settlements. Immediately arrest all suspects, interview them, and based on the gathered information react decisively." What is Colonel Mrksic doing in this order. Is he talking about infiltrators or is he talking about people who are disturbing the peace?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, for sure he identifies infiltrators because that we see from paragraph 2. And in paragraph 4, I mean, you -- it implies that you can only move if you have a freedom of movement pass. And, okay, these freedom of movement passes would be issued by the military, so the military would know who would have them and this would also allow to prevent the movement of unauthorised persons. And this could also involve volunteers or paramilitaries from Serbia who have not been authorised to move around or anybody else who hasn't been authorised to move around.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We would tender this document, Mr. President. I see the registrar shaking his head. It must be part of the package already. 00658, please, Prosecution tab 188.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This is again from the OG South Command dated the 21st November 1991 at 0600 hours in the morning. And before we look at the content if we can just go to page 2 and have a look at the addressees. Commander of the Seseljevci volunteers, Det. Commander of the Sumadinci Detachment from Kragujevac, and TO Vukovar commander. Now, first of all, on the 21st of November, 1991, what is the TO Vukovar? What does it comprise?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we know from the other documents we have reviewed before that it is a local Serb TO detachment that also includes volunteers or people affiliated with the SRS, the Serbian Radical Party of Mr. Seselj. And we know also that during the operations conducted by OG South that the TO Vukovar is subordinated to OG South through one of the three assault detachments that are established in the course of October 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Does it include any subsidiary TO units that are known by any name?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. According to -- I mean, a number of documents or several documents make mention of a TO Petrova Gora -- of a Petrova Gora TO detachment and a Leva Supoderica TO or Leva Supoderica Detachment; however, other documents also identify Leva Supoderica as a Chetnik detachment. When I say other documents, for example, documents of the Serbian Radical Party. And, for -- I mean, I mentioned that but I can repeat. The command of Leva Supoderica, Mr. Milan Lancuzanin, also known as Kameni, he's for example at a later stage proclaimed Chetnik Vojvoda by Mr. Seselj. Now I mention this because from the head -- addressees in the document, one would conclude that when mention is made of commander of the Seseljevci volunteer detachment that this actually refers to the Leva Supoderica Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's go back to page 1. And this again, the date is the 21st of November. It says: "In the course of 21 November 1991, withdraw the Leva Supoderica volunteers detachment and dispatch them, resubordinate them to the 12th Corps ..." Have I got all the extensions correct in that reading or not?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, that's correct. Yeah, it's subordinated or resubordinated to a brigade of the 12th Corps or a brigade subordinated to the 12th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you. So they're moving out of subordination from OG South and moving into subordination from the 12th Corps; is that right? Oh, sorry, the 12th Mechanised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether I need to tender this one, Mr. Registrar. No, I don't. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is also on page 485 in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 06031, please, which is Defence tab 331 -- 339.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This from the command of the 80th Motorised Brigade, the commander is Lieutenant-Colonel Milorad Vojnovic. It says to the commands of files: "Order." Point 2 says: "The Vukovar Territorial Defence Staff with the command of the 80th Motorised Brigade will establish organs of authority in local commune and organise their functioning, set up police stations, regulate movements of the population returning to town and their compulsory identification at the Velepromet reception centre." 3: "Relocate the Vukovar Territorial Defence Staff to a more suitable location near the Vukovar barracks as per decision of Commander Miroljub Vujovic." Let me just ask you there: When you look at items 2 and 3, would you infer that the Vukovar TO is still taking orders from the 80th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And it says: "The Vukovar Territorial Defence Staff in co-operation with the command of the 80th Motorised Brigade will prevent all forms of theft and misappropriation in the city of Vukovar and the surrounding villages." Does that look to you like a military administration?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, we have to look at the date of the document. It's the 22nd of November, so it's after Panic's order 2436-1. I mean, whether it's military administration or not, it's maintaining law and order which would be a task of town commands. Normally, obviously, it would be a task of the civilian authorities, but we are the 22nd. I would assume that Vojnovic has made his assessment on the state of functioning of the civilian authorities, and, I mean, the document doesn't talk about the civilian police but if he tasks the TO to be responsible for preventing all forms of theft and -- and misappropriation, it's his conclusion that the civilian police is not yet able to do so. It's not clear whether he has consulted with the civilian authorities about this, yes or no, from the document. I mean, he just gives a clear order to the local Serb TO staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Isn't it Mile Mrksic, the commander of OG South, who appointed Miroljub Vujovic on the 20th of November? Did he appoint the commander of that TO Vukovar staff?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen a document, I mean, that says what you are stating now. I understand that the 80th Motorised Brigade takes over the responsibilities of the Guards Motorised Brigade or OG South in the course I believe of the 22nd when the Guards Motorised Brigade is preparing to withdraw and to return to -- to its barracks in Belgrade and OG South is disbanded. But if you show me the document, yeah, then ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, let me remind you what you said in the Seselj case at page 4006 to 4007. And in one of your answers you say: "Now that we're at the Vukovar TO staff, I would like to make a correction to what I mentioned yesterday. I mentioned that Slobodan Katic had been removed at one moment as the person in charge of the TO for Vukovar, local Serb TO for Vukovar. I actually confused the name or the name of Katic with the name of Dusan Jaksic. It was Dusan Jaksic who was initially head of the local Serb TO Vukovar and at one time is replaced by a decision of the command of OG South by Miroljub Vujovic." Does that refresh your memory that, in fact, it was the OG South that appointed Miroljub Vujovic on the 20th of November?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does, Your Honours. And I apologise. I misunderstood Vujovic with Vojnovic in the previous question by Mr. Gosnell, so I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So sorry, just to clarify: The answer to my question is that it was --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- Mrksic who appointed him?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I would tender this document if it's not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honours. This document is already admitted on 11th January, 2013, as D20. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. If we could turn briefly to 06026, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And this, Mr. Theunens, is the key document that you referred to in your testimony, that, if I understand correctly, and you've now slightly modified your position, because now you say that this initiates a transition rather than marking an immediate shift of responsibility to the -- to the civilian authorities. Is my understanding of your additional nuance that you provided here today correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not a shift in position but, you know, there is the order and then it has to be implemented. Like, if you order to withdraw a military unit, for example, it's not going to happen in two seconds. So the order for withdrawal may be dated date X but it will take several days or even weeks or even months to implement the withdrawal, so that is what I tried to explain when I referred to order 2463-1; that is, that indeed it shifts the position of the 1st Military District, so this is 2436-1 of the 20th of November, because for the first time the 1st Military District recognises the organs of the SO or the SAO SBWS as relevant, i.e., legal, local authorities or organs of authority, and he explains then what kind of relations the -- the units of the 1st Military District should maintain with these SO SBWS authorities. But of course the practical implementation, as we also see from the documents, the documents going up to spring 1992, they show that it takes time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That's a fair point and I appreciate that clarification.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And the reason I ask it is because if you look at this very order, what I suggest to you is we still see the JNA purporting to exercise authority in respect of civilian affairs. The very third -- the third sub-point under 2 says: "Establish civilian authorities, take steps to establish law and order (safety of citizens, basic supply functions, and other communal needs) needs." And then the next sub-point is: "Work to establish civilian authorities in municipalities ..." So wouldn't you agree, Mr. Theunens, that we're still seeing a very healthy role being carved out - and I would suggest to you a dominant role being carved out - by the JNA in respect of civilian affairs?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, the fourth point, as well as other points in the report -- in the document, I'm sorry, in the order by Panic actually show that the JNA has a supporting role. They may still have the leading role in areas where civil authorities are not capable yet, for example, maintaining law and order, but it is conducted in accordance with decisions of the SO SBWS, and its -- its various organs of authority up to the municipal level.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's see if the documents show that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 06032 which is Prosecution -- or, sorry, which is P1683, Defence tab 421.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And this is from Colonel Milan Belic, a name that pops up --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- several times. And he is from -- he is the commander of the command of the town of Ilok which certainly appears to still exist on the 23rd of November 1991. And point 2: "Territorial Defence units are carrying out set tasks in their redeployment areas, i.e., securing settled area, communication routes, and vital installations, to ensure normal living and working conditions in those areas." Now when he says set tasks, would you agree with me that that implies those task have been set by the town command?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So as of the 23rd of November, 1991, would you agree that that -- those TO units are still subordinated to the JNA?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, as far as this document is concerned, discussing the situation in the area covered by the town command of Ilok and for the specific tasks, yes. Or for the set tasks, I'm sorry, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Second portion of item 3: "A military police detachment arrived in the village of Bapska from the Sremska Mitrovica municipal TO staff. A police station numbering 15 officers was established in the village of Lovas." Who do you think established that police station, based on that sentence?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It -- to me it's not clear that ideally we would have an additional document. There may be a document from the SAO SBWS if they had documents on this, but we would look for additional information as to -- in order to establish who is responsible for setting up this -- this -- this police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Point 7: "Intensive normative work is being done on establishing local commands and ensuring their functioning. In the course of the day, paramilitary organisations from the Dusan Silni Detachment were chased out of the village of Lovas and parts of the local TO were placed under a sing the command of TO commands present in the area." Now, doesn't that look like it's the JNA that's organising and setting up and commanding the TO commands present in the area?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's for sure playing a role in that. I mean, and it -- the fact that only then the Dusan Silni Detachment is being removed raises a number of questions because they were involved -- allegedly involved in crimes much earlier. So I mean here the answer would be yes, but obviously the local organs are also involved in establishing these structures, but here it's clearly highlighted that JNA is playing a role.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: By local organs here you're referring to municipal or town authorities?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: For example -- yeah, but it's -- I mean, it's not -- I agree with you, it's not mentioned in the document, but they obviously play a role in this because the manpower has to come from somewhere and so on, so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: A role, a directing role; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot state that on the basis of this document here. I mean, as you highlight, there is a directing or leading role of the JNA in this particular context.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: No mention at all here of any district authorities having anything to do with it, right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 06034, which is Prosecution tab 563. This is another document from our Colonel Milan Belic, commander of the Ilok town command. This is dated the 28th of November, 1991. So this is eight days after the 20th of November document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And it says -- at item 1 it's referring to the departure of civilians and the -- a number of abandoned houses or flats. Item 2 says: "The Ilok town command, which is responsible for the territory of the aforementioned settlements, i.e., Ilok, Lovas, Opatovac, Mohovo, Sarengrad, and Bapska, is receiving requests from refugees from towns and settlements in Eastern and Western Slavonia to move into the abandoned houses in Ilok and other aforementioned settlements. These requests are numerous and their number is increasing." 3: "Since the Ilok town command has no [sic] instructions or letters as to what should be done in such cases, we hereby request an explanation and instructions on how to deal with the requests of people from those areas to settle here." Now, don't we see here Ilok town command taking primary responsibility for resettlement of refugees from Eastern and Western Slavonia in the area?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so, Your Honours. I'm sorry. Because what this document states is that the Ilok town command receives questions from -- from civilians and asks its superior command, i.e., the 1st Proletarian Guards Mechanised Division for instructions and they forward it to the 1st Military District as is written in -- there's a handwritten note on the top of the document, so this is what the document actually states.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We would tender that if it's -- I withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It's not part of the package, actually. Is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I discuss it -- this in the new report but which was not admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now it's tab 563. It is not part of the witness's report, the amalgamated report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Shall we admit and mark it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit D45. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm delighted to get one through. Could we have 65 ter 763 [realtime transcript read in error "0736"], please. This is not on our list. I informed the Prosecution this morning of our intention to use this document, so I'm not sure if there's an objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And actually I'm sorry to peel away from our issue of civilian control and civilian affairs and come back to TO. And this again concerns Miroljub Vujovic as the commander of the TO Vukovar, and this is from the command of the ... is that 0763?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is incorrect in the transcript. It should be 0763 not 0736. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now this is a report apparently on the wounding of Miroljub Vujovic by someone, and it's dated the 5th of December, 1991, from the command of the 80th Motorised Brigade. Does this kind of reporting indicate to you that Miroljub Vujovic who is the commander of the TO Vukovar is still subordinated to the JNA?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily. I mean, the document doesn't allow to draw a conclusion on that aspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: It suggests that, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I wouldn't -- it suggests -- it's possible because the reason why I have a doubt is, of course, looking at the context and also the fact that given the nature of the personality of Miroljub Vujovic and some of the members in the Vukovar TO, or local Serb TO, is that the JNA had an interest in -- in -- in keeping an eye on their activities and, for example, such an incident here is, it is relevant for the 1st Military District to know so because it could affect the law and order situation. I'm sorry. The law and order situation in Vukovar. So it doesn't necessarily imply or -- or provide any information on the subordination relation between Vukovar TO and the 80th Motorised Brigade at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And why would you say there's an investigation being carried out into the perpetrator if he's not subordinated?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because as I mentioned the -- the -- the JNA is interested in the activities of Vujovic and -- I mean, given the role of Vujovic and his group also during the conflict and at this stage, so they're interested because it can affect the overall law and order situation in Vukovar, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And he has been sent to the Military Academy for treatment as well; right? JNA institution, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true. But maybe that is -- it's not -- it's the -- the VMA is the military -- yeah, the military hospital. But it is probably the best medical facility where he can be treated. I mean, I'm not sure what -- about the state of medical facilities in Vukovar. I don't know why they didn't send him to Sid or to Novi Sad where -- because there may be military facilities there too where he could be treated so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, if you're suggesting that this report has been written because Mr. Vujovic is a troublesome character leading a volunteer group, does it make sense that he would be sent to the VMA?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, I mean, as we discussed a Vukovar TO unit is recognised as -- as a legal or a local -- I mean, a local Serb TO unit, so I don't -- and, i.e., member of the armed forces, so I don't consider it unusual that he would be sent to a military facility to be treated. It depends on the nature of his wounds. In Belgium people suffering from burns who have nothing to do with the military are sent to a military hospital because it's the best equipped facility for these kind of things, you know. I don't say that you are wrong but I just try to explain that these documents -- document at its face value -- I'm sorry, for the transcript, doesn't allow to draw a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And no CC here to any SBWS TO HQ or General Staff, is there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. And again that can mean different things. Maybe Vujovic informed them in another way or maybe they were already informed. Again, it doesn't allow to draw a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We would tender this document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit D46. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 06045, please, which is Prosecution tab 569, also known as P378.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This is again from Colonel Belic as the commander of the Ilok military -- well, as it says here, the military command of the town of Ilok. The date is the 9th of December, 1991. Point one at the bottom page 1 reads: "Civilian authorities have not been established to date in the town of Ilok or the villages of Sarengrad, Mohovo, Opatovac, Lovas, and Bapska ..." Let's just stop there. Assuming that that pronouncement -- well, whether that pronouncement is correct or not, the consequence of his statement that there are no local authorities is that the town command still exercises civilian control over those towns, right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Actually that the town command -- the military town commander is still responsible for conducting civil affairs in these towns.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And therefore that's probative that that's what they're doing, right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and these duties are explained in 2436-1 as well as in the SSNO instructions 588-1 and 588-2, which we don't have, and 588-3.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Because all those instructions say that if there's no local civilian authority in place, it's the town command that exercises civilian control; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. But I'm not sure whether these documents use the expression "civilian control." You would have to define it. I do know that these documents use the expression "civil affairs" and there's maybe a difference between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: What is the difference in your mind?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I -- I mean, you haven't defined what you mean by civilian control, but I think it goes beyond what is defined as civil affairs in the regulations I have mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now I'm just not sure what you mean. I mean, isn't it the case that the town commands are supposed to exercise - I'm not sure what to use? - authority in respect of civilian matters in the towns?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Yes, I would say the easiest is to use the language in the terminology that is used in the JNA documents. Then we avoid any potential confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's see what else this says. It goes on: "We have one person," then we go to page 2, "in each of the following places in charge of local committee matters in Ilok, Lovas, and Mohovo."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, which paragraph are we?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We're still at item --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We're still at item 1.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And item 1 is saying, and this is Belic speaking: "We have one person in each of the following places in charge of local committee matters in Ilok, Lovas and Mohovo." What do you think that suggests?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it corresponds with what I said. I mean, when you look at the various reports from the -- the various city commands after the 20th of November, 1991, in -- in -- in Eastern Slavonia, they conduct activities which corresponded with -- with -- civil administration or civil affairs and they are specified in -- in the regulations. I have mentioned SSNO instruction 588-1, 588-2, and 588-3. And just to come back to this document, when you look at paragraph 3, it also -- again, it shows that certain activities are also conducted under the authority of the SAO Baranja, so we really have to look at the specific documents to see how this gradual process I mentioned earlier of the hand-over of civilian organs of authority which are being established is taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's take a look of a paragraph 3: "A police station has been established in Ilok and one of its squads has been detached and posted to the village of Lovas formed by the MUP of Serbia and is now under the authority of the SAO Baranja, Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. In carrying out its tasks, the police station is subordinated to the command of the town of Ilok." Now, how do you understand this statement which on the one hand says the police station is subordinated to the command of the town of Ilok, and then on the other hand it says is now under the authority of the SAO Baranja, Slavonia, and Western Srem? How do you explain that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking in the context of SFRY armed forces military doctrine, it can mean that it's -- I mean, the police station is under the authority of the SAO Baranja, Western Srem -- Slavonia and Western Srem, i.e., they are providing the personnel. They're appointing the people, including the commander. They may well be setting tasks. However, when implementing these tasks, when carrying out its tasks, there is a -- as a document states, a subordination to the town command of Ilok. This may also imply that the town command of Ilok, i.e., the JNA, can give tasks to the -- to this police personnel but they are under the authority of the SAO SBWS. So I would assume just to finish off that there is a consultation between the town command and probably as we saw in the other document by General Panic a consultation between the town command of Ilok through its superior commands, i.e., at the end 1st Military District on the one hand and the SAO SBWS on the other hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Who do you think has the final say in how law enforcement is conducted? Assuming your interpretation is correct.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you ask how things are done, then this document would -- this document shows that in the town of Ilok, the how is determined by the town command. But it doesn't -- it doesn't state what they have to be done and there I would refer to the sentence that they are under the authority of the SAO SBWS.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, let me suggest to you another possible interpretation that reconciles these two apparently contradictory sentences. It's that the police station has been set up within the territorial jurisdiction of the SBWS but it's still the JNA that runs the police station. Does that seem like a plausible interpretation to you?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, because it wouldn't be consistent with the use of the expression "authority."

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have P1708, please, which is Prosecution tab 578.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And this, again, is Colonel Belic --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- as commander of the command of the town of Ilok. The date is the 23rd of December, 1991, and as of this date he is still referring in paragraph 1, is he not, to the area of responsibility of the command of the town of Ilok, right? So as far as he is concerned there is still an area or a zone of responsibility, correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it -- I mean the area in which -- it's a geographic area obviously focussed on the kind of tasks that the town command of Ilok is -- excuse me, conducting.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So are you now saying that there's different concept of zone of responsibility being used in this document than the one that you defined on Thursday last?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. I mean, the zone of responsibility there was in context of combat operations. Here we're talking about a town command. And, again, looking at the context. I mean, if I -- I tried to find in the brigade regulations, I think 1983 or 1984, whether the zone of responsibility as such is defined by the JNA but it is not. There is something like an area of operations is defined. It may well be that zone of responsibility is defined in other regulation but I haven't been able to establish that. So my answer now is focussed on the specific tasks of the town commands.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That's correct. That the brigade rules don't refer to a zone of responsibility. They only refer to an area of operations. But wouldn't you agree with me that we've seen many, many documents that show that the JNA's operations include enforcing security in places where units are and they include setting up civilian authorities. That's well within the purview of JNA activities, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the basis of the orders they receive from their superiors.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, we're looking at a fist full of documents showing that they're in charge or at least heavily involved in civilian affairs, aren't we?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, looking at the different timings and the different context and the actual contents of the documents, then we can understand how -- what kind of civil affairs they're conducting, how they do that, and I think what is very important in the context of my report, the relation with local organs of authority, i.e., the SAO SBWS organs of civil authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, item 6 says: "Further engagement of units will be done in accordance with the basic decision of the commander of the town of Ilok with the emphasis on checking tasks, combat control of the territory, and securing of inhabited places." So securing of inhabited places still seems to suggest that we're talking about a law and order function being discharged by the town command; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. And, again, the document doesn't say whether there is a civilian police or not, but for sure according to this document the JNA is taking care of these tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's go to page 2, please, which is -- and item 10: "Occupation of empty houses continues in the territory of the commands of the town of Ilok's area of responsibility. Occupation is done without knowledge or approval of the command of the town of Ilok. The Presidency of SAO SBWS [sic] has not given an announcement so far regarding the way and conditions of occupation, which places this commands into a very complex situation. At the same time, ethnic Croatian inhabitants are under pressure to leave this territory." Now, first of all, just from reading this --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And I do see the time Mr. President. Perhaps we should take a pause there and come back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Theunens, next break until 11 -- until 12.45. Have you been told that the parties will most probably require your assistance tomorrow morning as well at the beginning of the hearing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was informally informed by the Victims and Witness assistant, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, while we're waiting. At the end of today's hearing, perhaps we could briefly discuss the issue of whether we'll be sitting on Monday next week, the 27th. We've been trying to organise ourselves around the possibility of not sitting on that day, as was indicated, and we think that is doable but wanted to at least raise the issue with the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So we were discussing this document that's still on the screen in front of us, Mr. Theunens. And, first of all, do you agree that that first sentence, "occupation is done without knowledge of approval of the command of the town of Ilok," doesn't that imply that occupation should be done with the approval of the town command?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily, Your Honours. And again I base that answer on the other documents I are reviewed discussing the same topic. There's a whole sequence of documents including also a letter by Mr. Hadzic directly addressed to Colonel Belic --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, but that's my answer, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You could just say no and then we'll proceed to the next question.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now if we look at the last sentence there it says: "At the same time, ethnic Croatians inhabitants are under pressure to leave this territory." Now, he doesn't say in any way that they're under pressure from the Presidency or from the SBWS government, does he?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And the reason why I ask you that question, sir, is because I think we can agree that there's a difference between the second-last sentence and the last sentence. The second-last sentence, the SBWS government is being criticised for having failed to produce an announcement, I presume of policy, but then the last sentence concerns a different subject; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It -- it's a different subject but they may well be related. And looking at the context, I mean the other documents, I believe there is -- there is -- there is some relation between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But he is not making that allegation, is he?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is not making that in this specific document, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have P371, please, which is Prosecution tab 580.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This again is Commander Belic writing. Same position. On 25th of December, 1991, and the topic line is: "Report on the Settlement of People in the Zone of Responsibility of the Ilok Town Command." And he says - and I won't read all of it - but he says: "We realised that the settling of people would be the most important task, which will be accompanied by objective problems. However, I could not have anticipated the unjustifiable indolence and I would add the indifference of the government of the Serbian autonomous district would create a handful of unobjective difficulties." So here we see some harsh words about the district government. And if we can go to the very last paragraph of the document, which is page 4, I suggest to you that we see the reason for this criticism. He said: "Having realised that the problem can no longer be ignored, we took the initiative and contacted SAO representatives in order to put the situation in a real perspective so as to prevent more suffering and uncertainty among the refugees. My objective was to single out this problem alone, although we come across numerous other problems which we have been resolving with our own forces so far, mainly to the satisfaction of the command. I will regularly inform you about how the settlement is proceeding and if problems crop up." Now, isn't his main reason for criticising the government is as he says here because that indolence is causing "suffering and uncertainty among the refugees"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. Also based because of -- and based on the instructions he has given in his exchange of letters with Mr. Hadzic. I mean, Mr. Hadzic sends a letter on the 23rd of December to Belic to complain about certain issues of the resettlement -- to complain about certain issues of the resettlement of refugees in Ilok. Belic replies on the 25th of December. Given that context, Belic understands that the SAO SBWS authorities are responsible for decision-making in relation to resettlement and that the town command has a supportive or an assisting role in that matter, and according to Belic, the SAO SBWS authorities are not taking up their responsibility, so the JNA, i.e., he, has no other choice than to fill that gap.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Belic's complaint is not that Croats are being removed or that the policy is facilitating or encouraging that. Belic is complaining that the government's indolence is inflicting suffering on the refugees; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. In this document, he doesn't talk about the pressure on non-Serbs in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Bottom of page 3 which is the previous page.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least on -- sorry, at least the part as I see -- part of the document I see, he doesn't mention Croatian refugee -- non-Serbs in the area, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: "Unauthorised settlement of Ilok is widespread although this command has not issued a single permit. There is no point in describing the various cases, but this might have been done by SAO ministers Bogunovic and Ljubo Loncarevic, a former policeman who is now in Backa Palanka, and so on." Now isn't what Belic saying here is -- well, let's start first with this: Doesn't this clearly indicate that the town command does view itself as the authority for determining who settles in what houses?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, because in other parts of the document and in other documents Belic explicitly refers to a decision he expects from the SAO SBWS he authorities in relation to the resettlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Fine, he doesn't get that decision, and he takes over responsibility of the process; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that it is then that he becomes responsible because somebody else who should be doing it doesn't do it. I think he is confronted with a problem. He raises it the superiors, I mean, see the the document of the 17th of December 1991 we have reviewed. You haven't shown that document but there is a reply from the 1st Military District dated the 23rd of December with the number 2562-3 re-emphasising the responsibility of the SAO SBWS authorities in relation to resettlement. But in the meantime, I mean, Belic is confronted with a situation and he reports on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You say somebody else doesn't do it and yet in this very document it seems that two ministers are being accused of improperly doing it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. But, I mean, it is -- maybe there are some nuances in what we mean by "it." My understanding from the documents is that the SAO SBWS determines the criteria and other policy matters concerning the resettlement of Serbian refugees from other parts of Croatia or maybe from -- from Serbia even or even from Kosovo in abandoned houses in Ilok. The JNA, i.e., the city command -- sorry, the town command of Ilok has a supportive role to play because they have most of the manpower. They may -- I mean, to facilitate this process. In the exchange between Mr. Hadzic and Colonel Belic, i.e., first letter by Colonel -- by Mr. Hadzic on the 23rd of December to Belic, and then the reply by Belic on the 25th of December, this is confirmed. And Belic denounces or criticizes what he considers the lack of active role of the SAO SBWS even though they have this role but they don't fulfil it. But instead of a leading -- I wouldn't say leading but a -- the SAO SBWS fulfilling this role to the best of their abilities, they are not doing enough according to Belic but instead you have two members of the government who allegedly are doing something but that is probably not necessarily consistent with the kind of policy the JNA would like to have seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Go back to page 2 if -- if we could.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Here we see that the JNA has taken an inventory and Belic has taken an inventory of empty houses in the various villages of the area of responsibility of the town command. He says there: "About 150 have been moved into in Ilok without authorisation which will be emptied in the coming period and planned and organised settlement will be required." Isn't he saying he is going to remove the people who have been settled there to date and he is going to settle new people there in those houses?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree in relation to the -- the -- the activities mentioned but not in relation to who will be responsible, i.e., who will be in charge, and who will actually implement these activities. Because that is not specified in the document. I mean, not in this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 6059, please. Prosecution tab 581.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Again, Belic writing to Mr. Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm not putting the predecessor document up. It's not relevant to my point. There we see paragraph 2: "In the second paragraph of your letter, you showed that you grasp the essence of military engagement and the introduction of military rule because it is a fact that the liberation is followed by a stage of stabilising the situation and creating conditions to gradually establish civilian government which can later on assume their part of the [sic] work." First of all, the expression "military rule," is that something you've seen in other documents? What is "military rule"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it -- I mean, the concept of military rule I think we have to look at in -- as it is used here, we have to look at it in the context of the orders that are issued for the establishment of town commands and then the -- in addition, the instructions determining the role of these town commands, i.e., conducting tasks of civil administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if we can go to page 2, please. At the bottom of the page, starting with the sentence: "Naturally..." Belic says: "Naturally, it is very difficult to have to deceive people who have suffered and lay the blame on others, and I say this because we have heard very many serious criticisms of your government. I do not intend or need to use this correspondence to tell you how to deal with the most serious task at the moment, which is giving accommodation and providing for the refugees mainly because I am sincerely convinced that you personally have given priority to resolve it, and I do not doubt for a moment that you will use your personal authority to arouse your listless associates." Now, again, is Belic's concern here as expressed to Mr. Hadzic that the refugees be placed in accommodation as soon as possible?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. And it's consistent with the view I expressed earlier that he addresses Mr. Hadzic for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I believe this --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, is this already admitted?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Correct. This one was already admitted through Witness Nielsen pursuant to the Chamber's decision of 9 May 2013 yet to be assigned an exhibit number. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have P1709, please, Prosecution tab 584.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, sir, what I'd like to do now is show you a series of documents about one or two specific places and how the situation evolves over time in those one or two specific places so we can see how the notion of this transition from military rule to civilian authorities occurs on the ground. And you looked at this particular document during your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if we can go to page 7 of the English. Could we try page 3. We're getting closer. It could be the page after this. Hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, sir, do you remember you were shown a document - and I appear to have the wrong number - which was dated the 29th of December and it showed that Mirkovci was an inhabited settlement?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. I mean, I've been shown a lot of documents over the past days, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That's fair enough. For our purposes, it's not absolutely necessary to show the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 06069, please, which is Prosecution tab 588.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to suggest to you that this document give us a flavour of what local politics is like in this region at this time, and it's a petition from some members of a TO, in particular the Mirkovci TO. And these individuals are complaining about someone who they allege has taken over this town, and they say improperly. And it says there: "On 10 August, command of the staff was taken over by Vuksic Egic at a local citizens meeting attended by fewer than 150 people, mostly supporters of Egic." And then there are various allegations against him which I'm not going to go into it. But what is significant for our purposes is the perspective or the attitude of those who are criticizing. And here's what they say on page 2: "Locals who are on duty and keeping guard day and night cannot come to terms with the fact that they do not decide about anything, have no insight into the distribution of aid (food, clothing, fuel, money) and we are particularly troubled by the fact that the staff appoints people to leadership positions who are not only not opposing Ustasha authorities but also condemn what we did. These individuals have lost their status as refugees in Serbia and have not spent a single day keeping guard." Now we don't know the background to all this, but would you agree with me that it appears that these members of the TO are more radical in terms of their attitude towards their Croatian neighbours than those who they allege have usurped power in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, before answering, could I see again to whom this petition is addressed? Just to -- because I've seen the document, just to refamiliarise myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: It's addressed to the Mirkovci local commune council.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. To answer your question, it's possible. I mean, the use of terms like Ustasha, whereas, I mean, this refers to the Second World War, I've also noticed that in JNA documents, it could express a sentiment of or a point of view of radicalism among those who use it but that is as far as I can go. I mean, as you said we don't know the further context of this, but I just know that it's -- the TO members addressed to local civil authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you notice that this document is not addressed to the district authorities, is it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that is correct, but it's addressed to the local civilian authorities, so maybe there is a -- I don't know. I mean, there may be a subsequent one but it makes sense to address it to the local authorities. It's not addressed to the JNA, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I would tender this document, if it's not already tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit D47. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: 6073, please. Prosecution tab 592.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This is an order from the assistant to deputy federal secretary for national defence. And we seen an order appointing somebody named Colonel Radivoje Kasic, commander of town of Mirkovci. And then his staff. Can you tell us why this appointment is being made by the SSNO?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not -- it's not clear from the document, Your Honours, whether there were already town commanders in those locations before, but I have no reason to assume there were no JNA town commanders before because, again, the orders of the 1st Military District and of the various subordinate units, indeed, ordered the appointment of town commanders there. So for me it's a continuation of the earlier situation that for whatever reason there needs to be maybe a rotation in the -- the people fulfilling these tasks --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Theunens, maybe my question wasn't precise enough. I was wondering if you could tell us why this decision is being made at the SSNO level.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a follow up of previous ordered by the SSNO, but I think the other question is justified: Why does the SSNO have to order the 1st Military District to appoint officers as town commanders in an area where units of the 1st Military District are present unless this would concern officers who are not part of the 1st Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Is it possible that the reason for this appointment from a very high level is because, as it says at item 4, "the complexity of the situation and the fact that all activities could not be foreseen in the instructions and so forth"? Is it because this is perceived as a particularly contentious or fractious area?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a possibility. But I would have -- I mean, this a document I saw in September but I was not in the position, for example, to check the names of these officers and to look at their peacetime assignments. If they came from outside the 1st Military District, then that could have been an explanation as to why it's the SSNO that issues that order, because the 1st Military District cannot order officers to do something. They're not part of its composition. If they were indeed part of the 1st Military District at the time of the order, then obviously we'd have considered other factors and maybe what is mentioned in paragraph 4, adding that what is mentioned in paragraph 4 is again consistent with the various orders and reports we have seen for the 20 November to, say, January 1992 time-period concerning the establishment and functioning of SAO SBWS authorities in -- in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I would tender that one, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit D48. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: 06089, please, Prosecution tab 599.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'm not quite sure how this document appears. It's formatted in B/C/S. But the front page is -- appears to be an agenda that's being set by the chairman of the executive council of Mirkovci, Vukasin Egic, the man who was being complained about in the earlier document. And if we can just turn over to page 2 -- well, before I go on, it says: "Immediate tasks of municipal executive council and individual secretariats in the upcoming period to the development of civilian authority and assisting the JNA in overcoming possible difficulties." And then if we can just go over to page 2. And it's a handwritten and partly upside down, it appears, in the B/C/S. In any event, do you see on page 2 that -- is that Mico Delic apparently making some notes?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We see the name Mico Delic, Major-General Mico Delic commander of the 1st Mechanised Corps typed there, but I wouldn't be able to say whether this is his handwriting or not. It may well be. Maybe you have a witness to establish that but I'm not in a position to establish that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And whoever wrote it, the comment is: "Power wrangling in the entire territory of the local commune up to the municipal structures. People of suspicious qualities who have compromised themselves in their work so far (prone to looting and theft). "Pressures from individuals and organised groups to relocate certain citizens (individuals and groups)." Does it look as if this is an identification of problems in respect of the functioning in respect of this local commune? Does it look as if this is an identification of the problems in this particular commune?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if we go over to page 3, do we see that the author of this, whoever it is, is saying that: "The zone of responsibility of the 1st MK covers 35 settlements. Settlement commands have been established in all settled areas within the zones of responsibilities of units, and they are subordinated to local commands which cover three to four settlements." Then there's a description of the activities, including a detailed itinerary of communes to be visited. When you look at that, doesn't it suggest to you that the JNA is exercising is supervision over these communes?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see the word "supervision" or -- in the document or anything to that effect. In my view, this is consistent with the earlier instructions on implementing the tasks of -- of civil administration, assisting the SAO SBWS authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Who is going to have final say in case of disputes, such as that that seems to be brewing in this municipality of Mirkovci?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You ask the question in context to the specific document or the previous document that was addressed to the civilian authorities, I mean the petition that was addressed to the civilian authorities in Mirkovci?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether this document suggests that the authority to resolve contentious problems lies with the JNA town commands.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that in this document, unless I forgot to look at something.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I would tender this document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit D49. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 6098, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This is from the command of the 1st Military District, Colonel-General Zivota Panic issuing what is an instruction or an order. An order. It's an order. He starts off saying: "Lately there have been very many complaints and protests by the citizens of Vukovar municipality about the improper work of the commanders of TO of towns, the presidents of local communes, and other structures. Having personally looked at and checked the submitted complaints, I have been convinced in the authenticity and credibility of the information. "In spite of my explicit orders to halt the forcible expulsion of Croats and others, without having previously checked the settling process, looting and so forth, nothing has been done but instead these incident have been become more frequent and more cruel. In order to put an end to this barbarism by these vigilantes, I hereby order ..." And he gives a series of measures. Now can I just ask you, when you look at that page, page 2, doesn't that suggest quite clearly that it's the JNA that ultimately is the final arbiter in respect of disputes at these commune levels?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document as -- the parts we have seen so far do not indicate who is responsible for -- or who is the final, as you call it, arbiter of these disputes at the communal level, I assume. The document -- what I have seen so far of the document doesn't state that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: How about the order to relieve of duty all those who have been compromised and appoint through your orders personnel who have been screened and are loyal?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding would be that these are members of the local Serb TO. Where it could be disputed whether the JNA is responsible for that yes or no, I mean, if you look at the legislation as it existed prior to the war, it would be the responsibility of local authorities, but given the particular situation and the shortcomings in the functioning of SAO SBWS authorities, here one would conclude that it's indeed the JNA 1st Military District that can relieve members of the local Serb TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You limit it to local Serb TO but the previous line says: "Investigate the work of the commanders of towns and presidents of the local communes in rural local communes."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you for the clarification. So it would also include then JNA personnel. I mean, like JNA town commanders who haven't done their work in a satisfactory manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And presidents of local communes; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I haven't -- not seen any documents showing that the JNA, i.e., the 1st Military District relieved or could relieve local SAO SBWS authorities. So I could take your -- your claim at face value and then I would like to see other documents, i.e., was this implemented or not and how was it implemented, and then I could maybe be of more assistance, but at this stage this is the furthest I can go.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We would tender this document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit D50. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: P1715, please. Prosecution tab 608.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is from the civil affairs assistant commander, Novica Busic [sic] command of the 1st Proletarian Guards Mechanised Division. He is writing on the 22nd of February, 1992, and he is describing a meeting at the Mirkovci municipality. And we see that some officials from the municipality are in attendance, including the police station commanders, the commander of the TO staff of the municipality, and commanders of the TO staffs of the local communes. And on the JNA side, we see what I think you would agree is some very senior JNA officials. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the level of participation of the JNA is consistent with the earlier order, I think the Panic order of 2436-1 of the 20th of December -- excuse me, 20th of November, 1991, where he explains who should maintain relations with who. It could be questioned, of course, I mean, referring to your question why the assistant commander of the civil affairs of the corps has to be present at a meeting at -- I mean, Mirkovci is a rather small municipality. It's not the size like -- a town like Ilok or so. It could be questioned, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, Major-General Mico Delic is there. Isn't that is a very senior JNA official?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I didn't see that. You know, I just saw the subparagraph B where Delic was not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: In fact Major-General Delic is leading the meeting, is he not?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what the document states, yep. It would be unusual, again in the context of the other documents, to have a corps commander present at a meeting with the local authorities at the level of a municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And the focus was on "resolving organisational issues related to the functioning of civilian authorities, TO, police units, and general organisation of daily life."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is indeed what paragraph 3 states.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you think that means that the JNA is sitting there passively and with a hands-off attitude receiving information but then ultimately not having a supervisory function in relation to those issues in this municipality?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I have mentioned earlier, it is my conclusion based on the documents I reviewed that after 20th of November the JNA has an assisting role and that the SAO SBWS authorities should have the lead. What I mean by should is that obviously from the various examples there are parts of SBWS where these SAO SBWS authorities have problems to assume that role, but, again, the various JNA instructions and orders reconfirm that the JNA has an advisory role and supports the local civilian authorities. I know that this document -- I mean, on the next page you will see that something else is suggested, i.e., that the JNA has the lead, but I see that document more as an exception to the other ones -- compared to the other ones I have seen than the document setting the situation for the other municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's go to the next page. And, first of all, we see that there is still a zone of responsibility in existence; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. But it's logical. I mean, even in a town command the commander has to know for which area he is the town commander. So it's a geographic area.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And the civilian affairs of the civil affairs organ is proposing for measures to be taken at the level of the government of the Eastern Slavonia, Western Srem, and Baranja SO to quickly resolve the issue of settlement in areas that were hitherto unsettled.
