And to more effectively change the national makeup in places already settled. Now do you see, can you see, when you look at that, can you see that the JNA is complaining that the district government, according to the JNA, has not in its view effectively changed the national makeup of places already settled?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that the -- the organs for civil affairs makes a proposal. I would say the wording is fairly neutral. I do agree with you that the organs for civil affairs proposes that measures would be taken by the government of the Eastern Slavonia, Western Srem, and Baranja Serbian district to more effectively change the national makeup in places already settled, which to me indicates that the -- the SAO government is responsible for decision-making in that domain.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: The JNA is dissatisfied, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, it's possible. I -- I don't see that they are dissatisfied. As I said, I find the wording neutral. They raise a number of issues where they want the SAO SBWS government to -- to take up its responsibilities. Or where they propose, sorry, the SAO SBWS government to take up its responsibilities. And, again, I just see, like, ten lines of the document. Maybe you can point me to those sections where dissatisfaction or -- and similar negative feelings are expressed by the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And no representatives from the district government are present at this meeting according to the document, are they?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 6113, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now the cover page. As I understand it, you've looked at this document, sir, during your examination-in-chief. And there's a cover page from Commander Major-General Mico Delic. And this from the 1st Mechanised Corps to the 1st Military District Command, and attached to that cover page appears to be a report by this Novica Gusic, the same person who we before. And it appears to, although there is no date on the attachment, the cover page seems to imply that this is going on at the end of February. If we can go to page 6, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, you drew some inferences about this document. I think we need to go back one or two pages in the English, please. I'm looking for item 10 in the English. So back one more page, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And this document says: "Because of distrust --" And this is this Gusic individual writing: "Because of distrust and what is happening to the Serbs who remained in Western Slavonia and their property and with the tacit consent of the government of the Serb autonomous district, Slavonia, and the assistance of the detached members of the government, the so-called co-ordinators and ministers ... are exerting certain pressure on the local inhabitants so that they would move away voluntarily. In doing so, they resort to unlawful means, threats, and have even killed some individuals." Now, can you first of all agree that what that passage is saying is that there's someone who's doing it actively on the one hand, and on the other hand you have what Gusic says is the tacit consent of the government of the SAO Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assumed that by "it" you mean the removal or the pressure on non-Serbs to leave?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, first of all, it doesn't actually say non-Serbs. It says exerting certain pressure on the local inhabitants." And that's what I mean by "it."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Okay, but -- yeah, that's -- I mean, fine. Again, when I say the non-Serbs, that's also based on my review of the other documents. And, again, most of these documents we have been looking at for the past hours are all new documents which I reviewed in the new report. It would have been easier to establish the context of these documents by having that new report in front of me, but I guess so is life. I'm sorry for this digression. I go back to the question. Again, based on the context we are talking about -- mainly about non-Serbs and there is pressure on them to leave. My understanding is that the reference to the Slavonia government when you look at the rest of the sentence, is not any SAO government in Western Slavonia but is, indeed, the government in the SAO SBWS. And that members of that government, even as is stated there, prominent members of that government are involved in this process of exercising a pressure on local inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Next sentence reads: "Characteristic examples of such conduct can be found in the villages of Bapska, Lovas, Sarengrad, and Mohovo, organised by Radojcic from Lovas village, the commander of the Lovas Territorial Defence Staff and co-ordinator for the TO 5th Zone who has a certain Ljuban Devetak, who is very influential in the government of the SAO Slavonia, standing behind him." Now first of all, isn't the commander of the Lovas Territorial Defence Staff subordinated to the JNA at this stage?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to doctrine it may well be the case. We don't know who appointed Radojcic. So, yeah, that's all I can say. The document doesn't indicate who -- to whom he is subordinated at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And SFRY imminent threat of war is still in effect at this date; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to remember. I think -- it was lifted at moment, but I think you're right, it was lifted at a later stage. So if the state of imminent threat of war is still in effect, then indeed the commander of the -- I mean, Radojcic would still be under the command of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And why is Gusic talking about the tacit consent of the district government in talking about his own tacit consent?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your proposition, his own tacit consent.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: He is subordinated -- if Radojcic is subordinated to the JNA, that must mean the town command in the area where that TO commander exists, and he is subject to the jurisdiction of that town command. Why isn't Gusic talking about his own tacit consent for this bad behaviour by Radojcic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that this is not -- this is an incorrect interpretation of SFRY armed forces doctrine because Radojcic would be subordinated to the JNA for the execution of specific tasks which would be set out in orders issued by the JNA units in the area where the TO was present and obviously to whom the TO was subordinated. What Radojcic is allegedly doing in the relation to the presence of -- to the pressure on local inhabitants, I haven't seen any JNA documents ordering Radojcic or any other TO commander to put pressure -- to exercise pressure on the local population.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, in a state of imminent threat of war, isn't the commander of the Territorial Defence Staff directly subordinated to the JNA?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the various documents we have discussed since -- I mean, basically also in the examination, and the repetitive orders by the commander of the 1st Military District to exercise military control and to subordinate the TO to the JNA and so on and so on show that the situation is not as clear-cut as Mr. Gosnell tries to depict it here, especially once the combat operations are finalised. We are now -- this is 22nd of February, 1992. There are no more combat operations in -- in the territory covered by the SAO SBWS, so again I would prefer to look at additional documents in order to establish what the subordination relationship is between the SAO SBWS and the JNA, and then specifically who was the commander of Radojcic at that time. So just to finish, this being said, obviously there would be responsibility on the JNA not just to write about in very quite vague terms about the role or alleged responsibility of Radojcic in putting pressure on local inhabitants. One would expect more detailed reports from the military police and/or the security organs. Maybe they were there, I don't know. I haven't seen them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I put it to you that whether or not there are combat activities as such ongoing is completely irrelevant. We know that amongst the JNA tasks, amongst the purview of the JNA's tasks, is setting up civilian authorities. So if you have a TO commander in an area in a zone of responsibility who has been charged with that and who is giving instructions -- is being given instructions by the JNA to do that, why isn't that person continuously subordinated in the discharge of those functions?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, if you can show me a document that indicates that Radojcic, and maybe I missed it, but if you show me a document that Radojcic is appointed by the JNA as a town commander or part of the town command in Lovas, then I would obviously review my answer but I haven't seen such a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So none of the documents that you've seen so far in respect of the relationship between the JNA and the TO would lead you to the reasonable inference that Radojcic has also been appointed by the JNA along with others who we have seen were appointed by the JNA in other documents?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that -- that people like Vujovic and maybe others have indeed been appointed by the JNA, but I -- again from the context of the other documents, it is my understanding that other local Serb TO commanders are appointed differently. And maybe -- and by other authorities. And again, I haven't seen a specific document for Radojcic, so it would be helpful to have a document concerning his appointment and then we can clarify the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you have any information or documentary evidence that confirms that Ljuba Devetak is in fact or was in fact very influential in the government of the SAO Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What I know about Devetak is that he was allegedly involved in the crime in Lovas in fall 1991, and I think he has been sentenced in 2010 or 2012 by war crimes court in Belgrade, he and others for his involvement in that -- in that crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we look at item 11.2: "The problem of mutual usurpation of power that exists between the police and the TO can be solved with more resolute stands by the government of the Serbian district Krajina, the MUP of Serbia, and the command of the 1st Military District." Do you know what that's a reference to and why is the MUP of Serbia being invoked?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The MUP of Serbia is invoked because there's personnel from the MUP Serbia that serves in the local Serb police as well as in the TO, and I'm not sure whether the process already starts then, but we are in this process of establishing -- of further establishing local Serb TO units based on orders from the SSNO and then the gradual transformation or the transformation of these TO units into police units in order to circumvent the Vance Plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: If I could, I'd like now to go to the last page of this document. I'm sorry, we're going to have start on the previous page. Down at the bottom there's a note, and it's talking about Egic and Tesic. You remember we saw that letter of complaint about Egic from those members of the TO who were complaining that he was, at least from their perspective, not sufficiently radical in terms of Ustashas as it was put in that document. Now that's just a preamble, sir.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't said that he was not sufficiently radical.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sir, I didn't say that you did. I'm just setting up the question. And what it says here is: "Both these individuals were appointed by the government of the SAO Krajina but the people do not accept them because in their work so far they engaged in dirty and illegal affairs, stealing, trade, and even physical pressure against the will of the people of which, according to statements from some local inhabitants and local organs of authority there is factual evidence. We believe that they should be removed from these posts and from the village all together through your influence on the government of the SAO Krajina." Now, first of all, I want it to be clear that we don't accept that this proposition that Mr. Egic was in fact appointed by the district government. But my question is: Wouldn't you agree that this kind of notation and the description of the situation as a whole, doesn't it raise some serious problems if you're trying to adopt a policy that is the most protective to the Croatian inhabitants because of this infighting, this factionalism, and frankly the strong motives by some groups to undermine those who have been pointed to positions of authority, for whatever reason?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just to allow me to understand the question. The "you" refers to Mr. Hadzic and the SAO SBWS government?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: No. I was referring to how the JNA is going to react to the situation.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the problem the JNA is facing, or at least as it is highlighted by Colonel Gusic, is that the SAO SBWS have appointed people who involve -- who participate in crimes and for that reason are not accepted by -- by the population. And then it is suggested here that the JNA exercises or uses -- I mean, the person, the addressee, uses his influence among members of the government of the SOWS -- sorry, SAO SBWS in order to have removed these -- these doubtful people or these -- these people who are allegedly involved in crimes from their position. Now I haven't seen -- maybe they were removed, but then it would be helpful if I would see such documents. I haven't seen any documents from Mr. Hadzic or members of the SAO SBWS to remove people except one document I think from January 1992 concerning the removal of the Leva Supoderica TO unit whereby Mr. Hadzic authorises the JNA to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, that is beyond the scope of my question. And I'll just go to -- first of all, I would like to tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit D51. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 6118, please, which is Prosecution tab 617.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. Before we move the document away, I noticed a little error in the last paragraph. If we go back to the previous page in the English version, it appears that the term SAO Krajina is being used interchangeably. In the B/C/S version if you look the fifth line it says "Vlade SAO Slavonija [phoen]," so we'll -- we can ask for a revised translation of this document. Just to put that on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] You would do that immediately, Mr. Demirdjian, so that we don't have to note that in our agenda as something to be done?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: To be done. I'll request it right away and hopefully that work can be cleared today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: 6118, please, that's Prosecution tab 617.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, this is from the 1st Military District. It's dated the 8th of March, 1992, signed by the head of the civil affairs organ, Colonel Jovo Blazinovic? And it appears to record a meeting. Do you agree with me that this meeting is between the civil affairs organs of the JNA of the 1st Military District and municipalities of the Serbian District of Baranja, Eastern Slavonia, and Western Srem, in order to ensure establishment of authority; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That -- that is correct, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So it doesn't appear that there's a district government authority -- representation at this meeting, is there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And, I mean, from what I see on the screen I don't know whether -- I cannot establish whether any -- any reference is made to the SAO SBWS government. Or, sorry, and in that stage, I mean, we are talk about RSK government.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: It says: "The following measures and tasks were agreed upon at the meeting of civil affairs organs of the 1st Military District and presidents of the municipal executive councils from the Baranja, Eastern Slavonia, Western Srem SO." And the first agreed upon item is: "Implementation of certain decisions that have already been planned and adopted, i.e., return of unlawfully confiscated land and other -- or other types of property, appointment of new individuals to certain positions within the TO to replace individuals holding those positions now as a result of specific elections procedures, prevention of power-wrangling, and refusal of practices introduced by appointees." And this is March 1992. Is the JNA still exercising dominant influence or very significant influence over the -- over these matters?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only say that the document refers to a meeting and an agreement on measures and tasks. It doesn't specify how this agreement was achieved.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if we can turn the page. At the top of the page, it says: "With a systemic development of the TO, including, among other things, the appointment of active duty personnel to TO staffs and brigade commands, the shutting down of local TO staffs (and provision of materiel and other equipment), the JNA will resolve other issues as well, including the separation of the TO from civil authority, et cetera." Does it look like the TO -- or the JNA is talking about inserting its own officers to lead the -- any existing TO structures?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. And this has to be seen in context of the instructions of the SSNO to establish an RSK TO, and we have seen other documents. I think the Prosecution also discussed some of those with me. And I also I note that, I mean, explicit mention is made to separate the TO from civil authority which to me is consistent with what we have discussed earlier; that is, that in the prior period - and we have discussed municipalities like Mirkovci where this poses problems - that civil authority, i.e., the SAO SBWS authorities maintained ties with certain individuals in the TO and even appointed people in a senior position the local Serb TO, whereby these people were allegedly involved in crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We would tender this document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit D52. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: 6122, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This is two days later. It's an order from the 1st Mechanised Corps Command, the assistant commander for civilian affairs, Colonel Novica Gusic. "Order: Re: Joint measures and activities by the civil affairs organ and the organs of the authorities to further constitute the authorities." So even now we're still talking about to further constitute the authorities. And task number 1 is that: "Town commanders," so the JNA town commanders, "together with the presidents of the municipal executive councils, municipal TO staffs, and brigade commands, civil affairs organs, inspect the following in their own territories: Local TO staffs, local communes, police stations, and other structures of the authorities, primarily those which are seizing the responsibilities of certain organs and structures of the authorities, on these occasions they shall interview the entire group, tell them about their location, role, and function, and make an energetic demand for them to reduce their activities to the framework of their prescribed responsibilities." Now, doesn't it look there as if the JNA is taking a directing role in the affairs mentioned there? In particular the appointments to the local TO staffs and the police stations.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could ... could I please see the first page of the document again?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And we do see on that first page that it does concern Mirkovci, amongst others.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't talk about, I mean, what I see here paragraph 1 and maybe you should now move to the next page to see paragraph 2. What I was trying to find out whether he talks about appointments of personnel. No, Your Honours, I mean, it doesn't talk about appointments of local TO staffs and police station. It talks about inspecting them. And it's done in, I would say, a collegial manner, i.e., the town commander with the presidents of the local municipal executive councils, so I think this is still consistent with -- with the role of the JNA as it was defined before, i.e., to assist the local authorities. And when I say defined before, after the 20th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Just one last question, Mr. Theunens. You don't think that the JNA being responsible for interviewing the entire group and making energetic demands for them to reduce their activities suggests supervision, control, direction?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, could we go back to -- to the bottom of the first page? Because it says -- I mean, on the second page, "they shall interview." I'm try -- just to make sure --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yeah, and the "they" is clearly town commanders.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, but, you know, look at title one. It says: "Together with the presidents of the municipal executive councils, municipal TO staffs, and brigade commands." So it's not just the JNA. It is the JNA together with local civilian authorities and officials of the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And in a situation like the one that we've seen in respect of Mirkovci with various power factions, factions struggling for power, who is going to resolve that in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I forgot to -- sorry, the reference for the previous document, but the previous document we saw there, it was suggested by a senior JNA officer that the JNA would use its -- its influence with members of the SAO SBWS or SAO Krajina, but it comes to the same, would use that influence in order to make these changes in personnel because the document also said the two individuals we discussed had been appointed by the local civilian authorities, i.e., the SAO SBWS authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I think we have to leave it there, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gosnell. Mr. Theunens, we will see tomorrow morning at 9.00. In the meantime, you're still on your oath. You know what that means. Thank you very much. The court usher will escort you out of court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stringer, about the 27th, I must say I thought that the parties have been informed about what we decided after the -- the little discussion we had. You confirm now that there is a possibility not to sit that day, and that's what we will do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just with this minor caveat, Mr. President. The witness who is scheduled is an expert witness and would have to be -- have his evidence completed by noon on Wednesday of that week, the 29th. Now we think that's -- that's quite doable. It's -- it's certainly not going to be the -- the extensive kind of evidence that the Court -- the Chamber has seen this week and last. So we think that it's quite likely he can complete his evidence by noon on Wednesday without any difficulty even accounting for cross-examination, et cetera. But it's possible that we may face ourselves or we may be asking to sit a little bit longer on Tuesday just to make sure that that happens. His travel has been arranged, he's made all of his arrangements with his current employer to be back home by that Wednesday evening which would require him to leave -- or to be finished by Wednesday on noon. We think it is quite doable but I just wanted to mention the possibility of possibly having to sit a bit longer on Tuesday to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's -- we'll take that into account. Anything from the Defence on that matter?
